Talk Talk.name: Talk Talk
Talk Talk.summary: A London band active from 1981 to 1991 and led by singer Mark Hollis. They started out playing synth-pop and had international hits in the mid-1980s. Their later albums Spirit of Eden and Laughing Stock moved into experimental music shaped by jazz and improvisation, and those records are credited with helping to pioneer post-rock.

Metric.name: Metric
Metric.summary: A Canadian band from Toronto, started in 1998 by Emily Haines and James Shaw. Bassist Joshua Winstead and drummer Joules Scott-Key complete the lineup. They play indie rock with new wave and synth-pop elements. The band has won several Juno Awards, including Group of the Year in 2010, and has been shortlisted twice for the Polaris Prize.

studio_albums.title: Old World Underground, Where Are You Now?

New Order.name: New Order
New Order.summary: A Manchester band formed in 1980 by the remaining members of Joy Division after Ian Curtis died. Gillian Gilbert joined soon after. Mixing post-punk with electronic dance music, they became key figures in alternative dance. Their 1983 single Blue Monday is the best-selling 12-inch single ever, and they spent many years on Factory Records.

The Gun Club.name: The Gun Club
The Gun Club.summary: A Los Angeles band led by singer and guitarist Jeffrey Lee Pierce, active from 1979 to 1996. They mixed blues, rockabilly and country into punk, which helped shape punk blues and cowpunk. The group ended when Pierce died of a brain hemorrhage in 1996.

Ladytron.name: Ladytron
Ladytron.summary: An electronic band formed in Liverpool in 1999. The current lineup is Helen Marnie, Mira Aroyo and Daniel Hunt, and Reuben Wu was a member until 2023. They play synth-pop and electropop and take their name from a Roxy Music song. Destroy Everything You Touch is their best-known track, and they have also remixed many other artists.

Robert Plant.name: Robert Plant
Robert Plant.summary: An English singer born in West Bromwich in 1948, best known as Led Zeppelin's frontman and lyricist from 1968 to 1980. He then built a long solo career. Raising Sand, his 2007 album with Alison Krauss, won the Grammy for Album of the Year. In 2019 he started the acoustic group Saving Grace with Suzi Dian.

The Cars.name: The Cars
The Cars.summary: This Boston group formed in 1976 and blended new wave, power pop and synthesizer rock, with Ric Ocasek as its main songwriter. Its hits included Drive and You Might Think. The band split in 1988, reunited for a 2011 album, and entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2018.

Van Halen.name: Van Halen
Van Halen.summary: Van Halen was a hard rock band formed in Pasadena, California, in 1972 around the brothers Eddie and Alex Van Halen. Its lead singers included David Lee Roth, Sammy Hagar and Gary Cherone. The band sold more than 80 million records, joined the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2007, and broke up after Eddie died in 2020.

Foreigner.name: Foreigner
Foreigner.summary: Foreigner is a British-American rock band formed in New York City in 1976 by guitarist Mick Jones, with Lou Gramm as its original singer. It has sold more than 80 million records. Its many arena-rock hits include Cold as Ice, Urgent and I Want to Know What Love Is. The band joined the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2024.

Doobie Brothers.name: Doobie Brothers
Doobie Brothers.summary: The Doobie Brothers formed in San Jose, California, in 1970, led at first by Tom Johnston and Patrick Simmons. After Michael McDonald joined in 1975, their sound shifted from roots rock toward soft rock and blue-eyed soul. Black Water and What a Fool Believes both reached number one, and the band entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2020.

studio_albums.title: What Were Once Vices Are Now Habits

Ohio Players.name: Ohio Players
Ohio Players.summary: This funk and soul group from Dayton, Ohio, started out in 1959 as the Ohio Untouchables. The band was fronted by Leroy Sugarfoot Bonner and became known for provocative album covers. Fire and Love Rollercoaster both reached number one, and Funky Worm and Skin Tight were also hits.

Chaka Khan.name: Chaka Khan
Chaka Khan.summary: Chaka Khan was born Yvette Marie Stevens in Chicago in 1953 and first became known as the singer of the funk band Rufus. She launched her solo career in 1978 with I'm Every Woman and later had a big hit with I Feel for You. She has won 11 Grammys and entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2023.

studio_albums.title: What Cha' Gonna Do for Me

George Clinton.name: George Clinton
George Clinton.summary: George Clinton was born in 1941 in Kannapolis, North Carolina, and grew up in Plainfield, New Jersey. As a singer, songwriter, producer and bandleader, he led the Parliament-Funkadelic collective, which shaped 1970s funk. He launched a solo career on Capitol in 1982 and joined the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1997.

studio_albums.title: Some of My Best Jokes Are Friends
How Late Do U Have 2BB4UR Absent?
George Clinton and His Gangsters of Love

Electric Light Orchestra.name: Electric Light Orchestra
Electric Light Orchestra.summary: Jeff Lynne, Roy Wood and Bev Bevan formed this Birmingham rock group in 1970 to mix pop with classical-style orchestration. After Wood left, Lynne led the band through big-selling albums such as Out of the Blue. Lynne ended the group in 1986 and brought it back in 2014 as Jeff Lynne's ELO.

The Tubes.name: The Tubes
The Tubes.summary: An art-rock group formed in San Francisco in 1972, fronted by singer Fee Waybill and known for theatrical live shows. Their early song White Punks on Dope became their signature number. In 1983, She's a Beauty gave them a US top-ten single.

The Alan Parsons Project.name: The Alan Parsons Project
The Alan Parsons Project.summary: A British studio project set up in London in 1975 by producer and engineer Alan Parsons and songwriter Eric Woolfson. They made progressive and soft-rock concept albums on themes drawn from science fiction and literature, with hits including Eye in the Sky. The partnership faded after Gaudi in 1987.

studio_albums.title: The Turn of a Friendly Card

Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark.name: Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark
Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark.summary: A synth-pop band formed on Merseyside in 1978 by Andy McCluskey and Paul Humphreys. They had early hits with Enola Gay and the Architecture & Morality singles, and later found US success with If You Leave. McCluskey stopped the band in 1996, and the classic lineup reunited in 2006.

Smashing Pumpkins.name: Smashing Pumpkins
Smashing Pumpkins.summary: A Chicago alternative rock band formed in 1988 and led by Billy Corgan. Its layered guitar sound brought major success in the 1990s, and Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness went ten times platinum. The band split in 2000, Corgan revived it in 2006, and original members James Iha and Jimmy Chamberlin returned in 2018.

studio_albums.title: Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness
Machina II/The Friends & Enemies of Modern Music
Shiny and Oh So Bright, Vol. 1 / LP: No Past. No Future. No Sun.
Atum: A Rock Opera in Three Acts

Rodrigo y Gabriela.name: Rodrigo y Gabriela
Rodrigo y Gabriela.summary: A Mexican acoustic guitar duo, Rodrigo Sánchez and Gabriela Quintero, who started their career busking in Dublin. Their instrumental music draws on flamenco, rock and heavy metal. Their album Mettavolution won the Grammy for Best Contemporary Instrumental Album.

Death Cab for Cutie.name: Death Cab for Cutie
Death Cab for Cutie.summary: An indie rock band formed in Bellingham, Washington, in 1997 around singer-songwriter Ben Gibbard. They broke through with Transatlanticism, moved from Barsuk to Atlantic, and reached number one in the US with Narrow Stairs. In 2026 they signed with Anti-.

studio_albums.title: We Have the Facts and We're Voting Yes

Rocket.name: Rocket
Rocket.summary: Rocket is a four-piece rock group from Los Angeles that became an official band in 2021. Its sound draws on grunge, shoegaze and alternative rock. Alithea Tuttle sings lead and plays bass, and the lineup also includes Desi Scaglione, Baron Rinzler and Cooper Ladomade. The band is signed to Transgressive Records.

DIIV.name: DIIV
DIIV.summary: DIIV is a Brooklyn rock act that Zachary Cole Smith started in 2011 as a solo recording project. It later grew into a full band. Its music mixes dream pop, shoegaze and post-punk.

Aaron Hibell.name: Aaron Hibell
Aaron Hibell.summary: Aaron Hibell is an English DJ, producer and composer, born in 1996. He combines orchestral, cinematic arrangements with techno and trance. He is known for Benevolence, from the Tetris film soundtrack, and for a remix of a Billie Eilish song that spread widely online. He records for his own imprint, All Time High, and for Astralwerks.

Thunder Jackson.name: Thunder Jackson
Thunder Jackson.summary: Thunder Jackson is a singer-songwriter from Oklahoma City whose father worked as an Elvis impersonator. His self-titled debut album came out in 2020, followed by the Take Me Back EP in 2022, which features Chet Faker. His second album, Hello Stranger, was recorded at Sonic Ranch in Texas.

Maribou State.name: Maribou State
Maribou State.summary: Maribou State is an English electronic duo of Chris Davids and Liam Ivory, who come from Hertfordshire. They have been active since 2011 and record for Counter Records, an imprint of Ninja Tune. Besides several EPs, they have made three full-length albums.

Poolside.name: Poolside
Poolside.summary: Poolside is a Los Angeles act that began in 2011 and plays what it calls daytime disco, a mix of nu-disco, chillwave and synth-pop. Co-founder Filip Nikolic left in 2017. Jeffrey Paradise is now the only core member and performs live with a touring band.

Dire Straits.name: Dire Straits
Dire Straits.summary: Mark Knopfler, David Knopfler, John Illsley and Pick Withers started this British rock group in London in 1977. They mixed roots rock, blues and pop and have sold over 120 million records. They split for good in 1995 and joined the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2018.

Deep Forest.name: Deep Forest
Deep Forest.summary: Éric Mouquet and Michel Sanchez started this French electronic project in 1992, blending world music samples with ambient sounds. Sanchez left in 2005, and Mouquet has carried on. Their album Boheme won the Grammy for Best World Music Album in 1996.

The Cure.name: The Cure
The Cure.summary: Robert Smith and Lol Tolhurst founded this English band in Crawley in 1976, and Smith is the only member who has stayed throughout. Often tied to post-punk and gothic rock, they were most successful commercially in the late 1980s and early 1990s. They have sold over 30 million records and joined the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2019.

studio_albums.title: Kiss Me, Kiss Me, Kiss Me

Crowded House.name: Crowded House
Crowded House.summary: Neil Finn, Paul Hester and Nick Seymour started this band in Melbourne in 1985. Don't Dream It's Over became their biggest hit. They broke up in 1996, got back together in 2006, and returned in 2019 with a new lineup that includes Finn's sons. They are in the ARIA Hall of Fame.

Counting Crows.name: Counting Crows
Counting Crows.summary: Singer Adam Duritz and guitarist David Bryson started this California rock band in 1991. Their first album, August and Everything After, and its single Mr. Jones made them well known. They have sold over 20 million albums, and Accidentally in Love from Shrek 2 earned them an Oscar nomination.

studio_albums.title: Underwater Sunshine (or What We Did on Our Summer Vacation)

Shawn Colvin.name: Shawn Colvin
Shawn Colvin.summary: Colvin is an American folk and Americana singer-songwriter, born in South Dakota in 1956. Her first album, Steady On, won a Grammy for contemporary folk. Her song Sunny Came Home later won both Record and Song of the Year.

Phil Collins.name: Phil Collins
Phil Collins.summary: Collins, born in London in 1951, joined Genesis as drummer and became their singer in 1975. His solo career took off with Face Value in 1981 and brought many number-one singles in the 1980s. He has won eight Grammys and an Academy Award for Tarzan, and he has sold over 100 million albums as a solo artist and with Genesis.

Eric Clapton.name: Eric Clapton
Eric Clapton.summary: An English guitarist, singer and songwriter whose career runs from blues-rock bands of the 1960s through a long solo career that began in 1970. He played in the Yardbirds, Cream and Derek and the Dominos. He is the only artist inducted three times into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

Tracy Chapman.name: Tracy Chapman
Tracy Chapman.summary: An American singer-songwriter from Cleveland, Ohio, known for folk-based songs with social themes. Her 1988 debut album and its single Fast Car made her an international star and won her several Grammy Awards. She released eight studio albums between 1988 and 2008.

Ray Charles.name: Ray Charles
Ray Charles.summary: An American singer, pianist and bandleader, often called The Genius. In the 1950s he helped create soul music by mixing gospel with rhythm and blues. He later had major success with country, jazz and pop recordings. He died in 2004.

studio_albums.title: Modern Sounds in Country and Western Music
Modern Sounds in Country and Western Music Volume Two
Ingredients in a Recipe for Soul
Ray Charles Invites You to Listen
Brother Ray Is at It Again
Do I Ever Cross Your Mind
From the Pages of My Mind
Thanks for Bringing Love Around Again

Beastie Boys.name: Beastie Boys
Beastie Boys.summary: A hip-hop group from New York City made up of Mike D, Ad-Rock and MCA. They started as a hardcore punk band in the early 1980s. Their 1986 debut Licensed to Ill was the first rap album to reach No. 1 on the Billboard 200. The group ended after Adam Yauch (MCA) died in 2012.

Edie Brickell & New Bohemians.name: Edie Brickell & New Bohemians
Edie Brickell & New Bohemians.summary: A rock band from Dallas, Texas, fronted by singer Edie Brickell. Their 1988 debut album went double platinum on the strength of the single What I Am. After a long break the band reunited and released new albums from 2006 onward.

Big Head Todd and the Monsters.name: Big Head Todd and the Monsters
Big Head Todd and the Monsters.summary: A rock band formed in Colorado in 1986 by Todd Park Mohr, Brian Nevin and Rob Squires, who knew each other from high school. They first built a following by touring heavily in the Mountain West. They signed to Giant Records in 1993, and their album Sister Sweetly went platinum.

Barenaked Ladies.name: Barenaked Ladies
Barenaked Ladies.summary: Canadian pop-rock group started in Scarborough, Ontario, in 1988 by Ed Robertson and Steven Page. They topped the US singles chart with One Week and wrote the theme for The Big Bang Theory. Page departed in 2009, and the band entered the Canadian Music Hall of Fame in 2018.

Anita Baker.name: Anita Baker
Anita Baker.summary: American soul and R&B vocalist born in Toledo, Ohio, in 1958 and raised in Detroit. After singing with the band Chapter 8, she broke through with the 1986 album Rapture and the hit Sweet Love. She has won eight Grammy Awards.

studio_albums.title: Giving You the Best That I Got

Arcade Fire.name: Arcade Fire
Arcade Fire.summary: Indie rock band from Montreal, started in 2001 around Win Butler and joined by Régine Chassagne. Known for large ensembles and baroque-pop arrangements, they won the 2011 Grammy for Album of the Year with The Suburbs. Misconduct allegations against Butler emerged in 2022.

AC/DC.name: AC/DC
AC/DC.summary: An Australian hard rock band started in Sydney in 1973 by the brothers Malcolm and Angus Young. Bon Scott was their singer until he died in 1980, and Brian Johnson replaced him. They are one of the best-selling rock acts ever, and Back in Black is their biggest album.

studio_albums.title: For Those About to Rock We Salute You

ABBA.name: ABBA
ABBA.summary: A Swedish pop group formed in Stockholm in 1972 by Agnetha Fältskog, Björn Ulvaeus, Benny Andersson and Anni-Frid Lyngstad. They became internationally famous after winning Eurovision in 1974 with Waterloo. The group stopped recording in 1982 and came back in 2021 with the album Voyage.

10,000 Maniacs.name: 10,000 Maniacs
10,000 Maniacs.summary: Alternative and folk rock band founded in 1981 in Jamestown, New York. Fronted by Natalie Merchant, they were most successful from 1987 to 1993. Merchant went solo in 1993, and Mary Ramsey later took over lead vocals.

Laurie Anderson.name: Laurie Anderson
Laurie Anderson.summary: American experimental artist and musician born in Chicago in 1947, working across performance art, electronic music, film and multimedia. Her 1981 single O Superman reached number two in the UK, and later projects include United States Live and Home of the Brave. She became NASA's first artist-in-residence in 2003 and was married to Lou Reed.

studio_albums.title: The Ugly One with the Jewels

Genesis.name: Genesis
Genesis.summary: English rock band formed by pupils at Charterhouse School in the late 1960s. Led first by Peter Gabriel as a progressive rock act, they became a hugely popular pop rock trio of Tony Banks, Mike Rutherford and Phil Collins after Gabriel and Steve Hackett left. Their worldwide sales exceed 100 million records.

studio_albums.title: The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway

U2.name: U2
U2.summary: Irish rock band formed in Dublin in 1976 at Mount Temple Comprehensive School, comprising Bono, the Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr. They broke through internationally with The Unforgettable Fire and The Joshua Tree and later reinvented themselves with Achtung Baby. They have sold around 175 million records and won numerous Grammys.

studio_albums.title: All That You Can't Leave Behind
How to Dismantle an Atomic Bomb

R.E.M..name: R.E.M.
R.E.M..summary: American alternative rock band formed in Athens, Georgia, in 1980 by Michael Stipe, Peter Buck, Mike Mills and Bill Berry. Growing from college radio favourites into global stars with Out of Time and Automatic for the People, they helped define alternative rock. They sold more than 90 million albums before disbanding in 2011.

Dinah Washington.name: Dinah Washington
Dinah Washington.summary: American singer, born in Alabama and raised in Chicago, who moved fluidly between jazz, blues, rhythm and blues and pop and was nicknamed the Queen of the Blues. She sang with Lionel Hampton before a long solo run on Mercury, scoring a major crossover hit with What a Diff'rence a Day Makes in 1959. She died in 1963 aged 39.

studio_albums.title: What a Diff'rence a Day Makes!

Shirley Scott with Stanley Turrentine.name: Shirley Scott with Stanley Turrentine
Shirley Scott with Stanley Turrentine.summary: A pairing of Philadelphia Hammond organist Shirley Scott, known as the Queen of the Organ, and tenor saxophonist Stanley Turrentine, who were married from 1961 to 1971. They recorded a string of soul-jazz albums together for Prestige, Impulse! and Atlantic, mixing blues, gospel and bebop. Scott later taught jazz at Cheyney University.

studio_albums.title: Roll 'Em: Shirley Scott Plays the Big Bands

Blur.name: Blur
Blur.summary: English rock band formed in London in 1988 by Damon Albarn, Graham Coxon, Alex James and Dave Rowntree. They became leading figures of Britpop with Modern Life Is Rubbish, Parklife and The Great Escape, then shifted toward lo-fi and experimental sounds. Every studio album from Parklife onward has topped the UK chart.

Depeche Mode.name: Depeche Mode
Depeche Mode.summary: English electronic band formed in Basildon, Essex, in 1980, built around Dave Gahan and principal songwriter Martin Gore, with Andy Fletcher, Vince Clarke and later Alan Wilder among past members. They evolved from synth-pop into darker, stadium-filling music and claim over 100 million records sold. Every studio album has reached the UK top ten.

Rapsody.name: Rapsody
Rapsody.summary: Rapsody, born Marlanna Evans in 1983 in Snow Hill, North Carolina, is a rapper associated with 9th Wonder's Jamla label and later Roc Nation. She appeared on Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp a Butterfly, earned Grammy nominations for Laila's Wisdom, and won a Grammy for 3:AM with Erykah Badu.

The Smiths.name: The Smiths
The Smiths.summary: English rock band formed in Manchester in 1982 by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr, with Andy Rourke on bass and Mike Joyce on drums. Signed to Rough Trade, they became a defining indie act of the 1980s through Marr's jangling guitar and Morrissey's literate lyrics. They split in 1987 after Marr departed.

The Herbaliser.name: The Herbaliser
The Herbaliser.summary: London group founded by producers Jake Wherry and Ollie Teeba, making instrumental jazz-funk and hip hop with frequent guest rappers. They recorded mainly for Ninja Tune before moving to !K7 and other labels, and also toured as a live band. Their albums appeared between 1995 and 2018.

Blondie.name: Blondie
Blondie.summary: New York band formed in 1974 by singer Debbie Harry and guitarist Chris Stein, rising from the CBGB punk scene. Mixing new wave with disco, reggae and rap, they scored chart toppers including Heart of Glass, Call Me, The Tide Is High and Rapture. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2006.

Roberta Flack.name: Roberta Flack
Roberta Flack.summary: American singer and pianist from North Carolina who rose to fame on Atlantic Records in the early 1970s. Her number-one hits included The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face, Killing Me Softly with His Song and Feel Like Makin' Love, and she recorded celebrated duets with Donny Hathaway and Peabo Bryson. She died in 2025.

studio_albums.title: Friends: Roberta Flack Sings Mariko Takahashi
Let It Be Roberta: Roberta Flack Sings the Beatles

The Beach Boys.name: The Beach Boys
The Beach Boys.summary: American rock band formed in Hawthorne, California, in 1961 by brothers Brian, Dennis and Carl Wilson, their cousin Mike Love and friend Al Jardine. Famous for vocal harmonies and songs about surfing and California youth, they grew more ambitious under Brian Wilson's production, peaking artistically with Pet Sounds and Good Vibrations.

studio_albums.title: That's Why God Made the Radio

Yvonne Fair.name: Yvonne Fair
Yvonne Fair.summary: American soul singer from Richmond, Virginia, who sang with the Chantels and the James Brown Revue before joining Motown, where she worked with Norman Whitfield. Her version of It Should Have Been Me became a UK top-five hit in 1976. She later retired from recording and died in 1994.

Santana.name: Santana
Santana.summary: American rock band formed in San Francisco in 1967 around guitarist Carlos Santana, blending rock, blues, jazz and Latin percussion. Their Woodstock appearance and early albums such as Abraxas made them stars, and the 1999 comeback Supernatural sold tens of millions of copies. The band has sold over 100 million records.

studio_albums.title: Guitar Heaven: The Greatest Guitar Classics of All Time

100 Proof (Aged in Soul).name: 100 Proof (Aged in Soul)
100 Proof (Aged in Soul).summary: Detroit soul and funk vocal group assembled in 1969 by Holland-Dozier-Holland for their Hot Wax label, with singers including Steve Mancha and Joe Stubbs. Their biggest record, Somebody's Been Sleeping, reached the pop top ten and sold over a million copies. The group broke up in 1973.

studio_albums.title: Somebody's Been Sleeping in My Bed

Funkadelic.name: Funkadelic
Funkadelic.summary: American band led by George Clinton that emerged in the late 1960s alongside its sister act Parliament, together forming the P-Funk collective. Funkadelic fused funk with psychedelic rock and soul, producing landmark records such as Maggot Brain and One Nation Under a Groove. The group has been hugely influential on funk, rock and hip hop.

studio_albums.title: Free Your Mind... and Your Ass Will Follow
Standing on the Verge of Getting It On
Let's Take It to the Stage
The Electric Spanking of War Babies
First Ya Gotta Shake the Gate

Sault.name: Sault
Sault.summary: Largely anonymous British collective formed in 2019, led by producer Inflo and singer Cleo Sol, with collaborators such as Kid Sister and Michael Kiwanuka. Blending soul, funk, gospel and disco, they often address Black identity and protest. They release albums with little promotion and have won a MOBO Award and an Ivor Novello Award.

Earth, Wind & Fire.name: Earth, Wind & Fire
Earth, Wind & Fire.summary: American band founded by Maurice White in Chicago in 1969, combining funk, soul, jazz, disco, Latin and African influences. Known for kalimba, a powerful horn section, theatrical concerts and the pairing of Philip Bailey's falsetto with White's tenor, they have sold over 90 million records and won six Grammys. They are in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

studio_albums.title: That's the Way of the World

Josh White.name: Josh White
Josh White.summary: Singer and guitarist from Greenville, South Carolina (1914 to 1969), who began as a Piedmont blues recording artist and became a star of New York's folk and cabaret scene in the 1940s. He also acted on Broadway and radio and championed civil rights, but was blacklisted during the Red Scare. He entered the Blues Hall of Fame in 2023.

Wes Montgomery.name: Wes Montgomery
Wes Montgomery.summary: Jazz guitarist from Indianapolis (1923 to 1968) known for picking with his thumb and playing melodies in octaves and block chords. After acclaimed Riverside records such as The Incredible Jazz Guitar, he reached a wide pop audience with orchestral albums for Verve and A&M before dying of a heart attack at 45.

studio_albums.title: The Incredible Jazz Guitar of Wes Montgomery

Lee Wiley.name: Lee Wiley
Lee Wiley.summary: Jazz singer from Fort Gibson, Oklahoma (1908 to 1975), of Cherokee descent, who sang on network radio and with bands led by Leo Reisman and Paul Whiteman. She pioneered the songbook album, recording sets devoted to Gershwin, Cole Porter, Rodgers and Hart and other composers with leading Dixieland and swing musicians.

Carole King.name: Carole King
Carole King.summary: American songwriter and singer from New York who, with Gerry Goffin, wrote many 1960s hits for other performers before launching a solo career. Her 1971 album Tapestry became one of the best-selling records of its era. She has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame both as a songwriter and as a performer.

studio_albums.title: Pearls: Songs of Goffin and King

B.B. King.name: B.B. King
B.B. King.summary: Mississippi-born blues guitarist and singer, nicknamed the King of the Blues, whose fluid string bending and vibrato on his guitar Lucille shaped modern electric blues and rock. Active from the late 1940s until shortly before his death in 2015, he scored his biggest pop success with The Thrill Is Gone and won numerous Grammys.

studio_albums.title: To Know You Is to Love You
There Must Be a Better World Somewhere
There Is Always One More Time
Makin' Love Is Good for You

Supertramp.name: Supertramp
Supertramp.summary: English rock band formed in London in 1969, centred on songwriters Rick Davies and Roger Hodgson, who blended progressive rock with pop melodies and prominent keyboards and saxophone. After early struggles they broke through with Crime of the Century, and Breakfast in America became a global bestseller with hits such as The Logical Song.

Ahmad Jamal.name: Ahmad Jamal
Ahmad Jamal.summary: American jazz pianist, composer and bandleader born in Pittsburgh in 1930, who led small groups for about six decades until his death in 2023. His 1958 live trio album At the Pershing became a major seller, and his spare, rhythmically inventive style strongly influenced Miles Davis. He was named an NEA Jazz Master.

studio_albums.title: Listen to the Ahmad Jamal Quintet
The Bright, the Blue and the Beautiful

Bad Company.name: Bad Company
Bad Company.summary: English hard rock supergroup formed in 1973 by Paul Rodgers and Simon Kirke of Free, Mick Ralphs of Mott the Hoople and bassist Boz Burrell. Managed by Peter Grant and signed to Swan Song, they had hits such as Can't Get Enough and Feel Like Makin' Love. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2025.

Common.name: Common
Common.summary: Chicago rapper and actor Lonnie Rashid Lynn, who first recorded as Common Sense in the early 1990s and became known for thoughtful, socially conscious lyrics. He has won Grammy, Oscar and Emmy awards, the Oscar for co-writing Glory from the film Selma, and has acted in many films and TV series.

studio_albums.title: One Day It'll All Make Sense

Elton John.name: Elton John
Elton John.summary: English singer, pianist and composer whose partnership with lyricist Bernie Taupin began in 1967 and produced hits including Your Song, Rocket Man and Tiny Dancer. One of the best-selling artists in history, he dominated the 1970s charts and later wrote music for The Lion King. He was knighted and has won Grammy, Tony and Academy Awards.

studio_albums.title: Don't Shoot Me I'm Only the Piano Player
Captain Fantastic and the Brown Dirt Cowboy

James Brown.name: James Brown
James Brown.summary: James Brown (1933–2006), from South Carolina and Georgia, was a singer, bandleader and dancer known as the Godfather of Soul. His rhythm-focused records of the late 1960s and early 1970s were central to the creation of funk and became a major source of samples for hip-hop.

studio_albums.title: James Brown and His Famous Flames Tour the U.S.A.
James Brown Plays James Brown Today & Yesterday
James Brown Plays New Breed (The Boo-Ga-Loo)
James Brown Plays the Real Thing

Take a Look at Those Cakes

The Beatles.name: The Beatles
The Beatles.summary: Rock band from Liverpool consisting of John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr, active from 1960 to 1970. Led by the Lennon and McCartney songwriting team, they moved from beat music to studio experimentation on albums such as Revolver and Sgt. Pepper. They are the best-selling music act of all time.

studio_albums.title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band

Dionne Warwick.name: Dionne Warwick
Dionne Warwick.summary: American singer from East Orange, New Jersey, whose long partnership with songwriters Burt Bacharach and Hal David produced hits such as Walk On By and I Say a Little Prayer. Her career spans more than six decades, with later successes including That's What Friends Are For. She has won multiple Grammy Awards.

On Stage and in the Movies
Dionne Warwick in Valley of the Dolls
I'll Never Fall in Love Again
How Many Times Can We Say Goodbye
My Favorite Time of the Year
Dionne Warwick & the Voices of Christmas

The Steve Miller Band.name: The Steve Miller Band
The Steve Miller Band.summary: American rock band formed in San Francisco in 1966 around guitarist and singer Steve Miller. Starting in blues and psychedelic rock, they turned to radio-friendly rock in the 1970s with hits like The Joker, Fly Like an Eagle and Abracadabra. The group was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2016.

studio_albums.title: Recall the Beginning...A Journey from Eden

Thelonious Monk.name: Thelonious Monk
Thelonious Monk.summary: American jazz pianist and composer (1917 to 1982) who helped shape bebop in the 1940s and became one of the most recorded jazz composers. His angular melodies, dissonant harmonies and percussive playing appear in standards such as Round Midnight, Straight, No Chaser and Blue Monk. He recorded for Blue Note, Prestige, Riverside and Columbia.

studio_albums.title: Thelonious Monk Quintet Blows for LP
Thelonious Monk Plays the Music of Duke Ellington

Eagles.name: Eagles
Eagles.summary: American rock band formed in Los Angeles in 1971, central to the country rock and soft rock sound of the 1970s. Led by Glenn Frey and Don Henley, they released Hotel California and one of the best-selling compilations in US history. They split in 1980, reunited in 1994 and entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1998.

Willie Nelson.name: Willie Nelson
Willie Nelson.summary: Texas-born singer, songwriter and guitarist who began as a Nashville songwriter, penning Crazy for Patsy Cline, and became a leader of the 1970s outlaw country movement with Red Headed Stranger. Exceptionally prolific, he has released well over 70 solo studio albums and is also known for activism and acting.

studio_albums.title: The Words Don't Fit the Picture
The IRS Tapes: Who'll Buy My Memories?
You Don't Know Me: The Songs of Cindy Walker
Let's Face the Music and Dance
For the Good Times: A Tribute to Ray Price
I Don't Know a Thing About Love

Jon Batiste.name: Jon Batiste
Jon Batiste.summary: American musician and composer born in 1986 in Louisiana to a New Orleans musical family and trained at Juilliard. He led the house band on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert from 2015 to 2022 and co-wrote the Oscar-winning score for Pixar's Soul. His album We Are won the Grammy for Album of the Year in 2022.

Marc Hype & Jim Dunloop.name: Marc Hype & Jim Dunloop
Marc Hype & Jim Dunloop.summary: A Berlin partnership between DJ and producer Marc Hype (Marc Gärtner, a two-time German ITF turntablism champion) and classically trained pianist Jim Dunloop, who began playing together in 2004. Dunloop adds live piano to Hype's funk and hip hop sets, and the pair issued singles on Milk Crate and Melting Pot Music, including a cover of Babe Ruth's The Mexican.

The English Beat.name: The English Beat
The English Beat.summary: Birmingham band formed in 1978, known in North America as the English Beat, who combined ska, pop, soul and reggae during the 2 Tone era. Fronted by Dave Wakeling and Ranking Roger, they had hits such as Mirror in the Bathroom before splitting in 1983. Wakeling and Roger later led separate versions of the group.

Missing Persons.name: Missing Persons
Missing Persons.summary: A Los Angeles new wave band formed in 1980 by singer Dale Bozzio, drummer Terry Bozzio and guitarist Warren Cuccurullo, several of them alumni of Frank Zappa's band. Known for Dale Bozzio's striking look and voice, they scored early 1980s hits including Words and Destination Unknown.

Jefferson Airplane.name: Jefferson Airplane
Jefferson Airplane.summary: San Francisco rock band formed in 1965 and a leading voice of the psychedelic counterculture. With singers Grace Slick and Marty Balin, they reached the US top ten with Somebody to Love and White Rabbit and played Monterey, Woodstock and Altamont. Members later continued as Jefferson Starship and Hot Tuna.

It's a Beautiful Day.name: It's a Beautiful Day
It's a Beautiful Day.summary: A San Francisco band formed in 1967 and led by violinist David LaFlamme, mixing rock with jazz, folk and classical influences. Their signature song White Bird came from their 1969 debut, and the theme of their Bombay Calling was later borrowed by Deep Purple for Child in Time.

Big Brother & The Holding Company.name: Big Brother & The Holding Company
Big Brother & The Holding Company.summary: A psychedelic rock band from the 1965 San Francisco scene, best known for its period with Janis Joplin as lead singer. Their 1968 album Cheap Thrills became a national number one shortly before Joplin left for a solo career. The group split in 1972, and the classic lineup reformed in 1987.

Johnnie Taylor.name: Johnnie Taylor
Johnnie Taylor.summary: Arkansas born singer (1934 to 2000) whose career moved from gospel to soul, blues and disco. Billed at Stax as the Philosopher of Soul, he hit with Who's Making Love in 1968, and Disco Lady topped the Billboard Hot 100 in 1976. He later recorded for many years on Malaco.

studio_albums.title: I Know It's Wrong But I... Just Can't Do Right

Shirley Bassey.name: Shirley Bassey
Shirley Bassey.summary: Welsh singer born in Cardiff's Tiger Bay in 1937, famed for her powerful voice and a career spanning seven decades. She is the only artist to sing more than one official James Bond theme, recording Goldfinger, Diamonds Are Forever and Moonraker. She was made a Dame in 2000 and has sold well over 100 million records.

studio_albums.title: I've Got a Song for You
Sings the Songs of Andrew Lloyd Webber
I Owe It All to You

Wu-Tang Clan.name: Wu-Tang Clan
Wu-Tang Clan.summary: A hip hop collective from Staten Island, New York, assembled in 1992 by RZA, who also produced most of their music. Members including GZA, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah and Ol' Dirty Bastard built major solo careers alongside the group, whose 1993 debut is considered one of rap's most influential albums.

studio_albums.title: Once Upon a Time in Shaolin

Original Flavor.name: Original Flavor
Original Flavor.summary: An American hip hop group of the early and mid 1990s, built around producer and rapper Ski and managed by Damon Dash. They released two albums on Atlantic, and their single Can I Get Open featured an early appearance by Jay-Z. Ski went on to produce for Roc-A-Fella, including tracks on Reasonable Doubt.

UnkleJam.name: UnkleJam
UnkleJam.summary: A British electro soul and R&B group formed by Tendai Tyson and signed to Virgin in 2006, with a sound influenced by P-Funk, Prince and Sly Stone; the name nods to a Funkadelic album. After supporting Justin Timberlake in Europe, they reached number 16 in the UK in 2007 with What Am I Fighting For?

The Quantic Soul Orchestra.name: The Quantic Soul Orchestra
The Quantic Soul Orchestra.summary: A live funk and soul band project started in 2003 by English DJ and producer Will Holland, who is best known as Quantic. Recording mainly for Tru Thoughts, the group revived vintage funk and jazz grooves, worked with singers such as Alice Russell and Spanky Wilson, and later added Latin and Afro influences.

Black Moon.name: Black Moon
Black Moon.summary: A Brooklyn hip hop trio of Buckshot, 5ft and DJ Evil Dee, formed in 1992. Evil Dee's production team Da Beatminerz supplied their sound, and the group became the core of the Boot Camp Clik collective and the Duck Down label. Their 1993 debut is regarded as an underground classic.

Carly Simon.name: Carly Simon
Carly Simon.summary: American singer-songwriter from New York who rose to fame in the early 1970s with hits such as You're So Vain and Anticipation. She won the Grammy for Best New Artist in 1972, later earned an Oscar for Let the River Run, and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2022.

Hieroglyphics.name: Hieroglyphics
Hieroglyphics.summary: An Oakland, California hip hop collective founded in 1991 by Del the Funky Homosapien, also including Casual, Pep Love, Domino, DJ Toure and the four members of Souls of Mischief. The crew became a model of independent rap by releasing its music through its own Hieroglyphics Imperium label.

Nicky Hopkins, Ry Cooder, Mick Jagger, B.name: Nicky Hopkins, Ry Cooder, Mick Jagger, Bill Wyman, Charlie Watts
Nicky Hopkins, Ry Cooder, Mick Jagger, B.summary: This billing covers a one-off 1969 studio jam by English pianist Nicky Hopkins, American guitarist Ry Cooder and three Rolling Stones, Mick Jagger, Bill Wyman and Charlie Watts, issued in 1972 as Jamming with Edward! Hopkins (1944 to 1994) was a celebrated session player heard on records by the Stones, the Kinks, the Who and the Beatles.

studio_albums.title: The Revolutionary Piano of Nicky Hopkins
The Tin Man Was a Dreamer

Jackson Browne.name: Jackson Browne
Jackson Browne.summary: American singer-songwriter born in Heidelberg, Germany, in 1948 and raised in Southern California. He wrote songs for others, including co-writing the Eagles' Take It Easy, before his own introspective albums such as Late for the Sky and Running on Empty. A longtime activist, he joined the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2004.

Lauryn Hill.name: Lauryn Hill
Lauryn Hill.summary: Rapper, singer, producer and actress born in East Orange, New Jersey, in 1975. She first found fame fronting the Fugees, whose album The Score topped the US chart. Her lone solo studio album in 1998 made her the first rapper to win the Grammy for Album of the Year, and she holds eight Grammys overall.

America.name: America
America.summary: A soft rock and folk rock group formed in London in 1970 by Dewey Bunnell, Gerry Beckley and Dan Peek, sons of US Air Force families stationed in England. Hits such as A Horse with No Name, Ventura Highway and Sister Golden Hair made them stars, and they won the Grammy for Best New Artist.

Stevie Wonder.name: Stevie Wonder
Stevie Wonder.summary: Singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist who signed to Motown as a child prodigy in the early 1960s. His run of 1970s albums, from Talking Book to Songs in the Key of Life, earned him numerous Grammys, including three Album of the Year awards. He has sold more than 100 million records.

studio_albums.title: The Jazz Soul of Little Stevie
With a Song in My Heart
I Was Made to Love Her
Songs in the Key of Life

Martin Denny.name: Martin Denny
Martin Denny.summary: American pianist, composer and arranger (1911 to 2005), widely called the father of exotica. Based in Honolulu from 1954, his group blended Pacific, Asian and Latin flavors with bird calls and animal sounds, and his version of Quiet Village became a top-five US hit in 1959. He recorded prolifically for Liberty.

studio_albums.title: Quiet Village: The Exotic Sounds of Martin Denny
Exotic Sounds from the Silver Screen

Anita O'Day.name: Anita O'Day
Anita O'Day.summary: Born Anita Belle Colton in Kansas City in 1919, O'Day was a jazz vocalist celebrated for her rhythmic daring and inventive phrasing. She rose through the big band era and later made a long run of albums for Verve. She rejected the glamorous girl singer image and kept performing until shortly before her death in 2006.

studio_albums.title: Pick Yourself Up with Anita O'Day
Anita O'Day Swings Cole Porter with Billy May
Anita O'Day and Billy May Swing Rodgers and Hart
The Night Has a Thousand Eyes

Fats Domino.name: Fats Domino
Fats Domino.summary: New Orleans pianist and singer Antoine Domino was one of the founding stars of rock and roll. Working with producer and co-writer Dave Bartholomew on Imperial Records, he scored a long string of hits in the 1950s, including Ain't That a Shame and Blueberry Hill, and sold tens of millions of records.

studio_albums.title: Rock and Rollin' with Fats Domino

Pointer Sisters.name: Pointer Sisters
Pointer Sisters.summary: Vocal group of sisters from Oakland, California, raised by a minister's family, who debuted in 1973 with a jazz- and swing-influenced sound. Later working as a trio with producer Richard Perry, they had pop and R&B hits including Fire, I'm So Excited and Jump (For My Love).

Loverboy.name: Loverboy
Loverboy.summary: Hard rock band formed in Calgary in 1979 around singer Mike Reno and guitarist Paul Dean. They became one of Canada's best-selling acts in the early 1980s with arena-ready hits such as Turn Me Loose and Working for the Weekend, and continue to tour.

Creedence Clearwater Revival.name: Creedence Clearwater Revival
Creedence Clearwater Revival.summary: Rock band from El Cerrito, California, led by singer and songwriter John Fogerty with his brother Tom, Stu Cook and Doug Clifford. Between 1968 and 1972 they released a string of swamp-rock hits such as Proud Mary, Bad Moon Rising and Fortunate Son before splitting; they entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1993.

Richie Kamuca / Bill Holman.name: Richie Kamuca / Bill Holman
Richie Kamuca / Bill Holman.summary: A pairing of two West Coast jazz figures: tenor saxophonist Richie Kamuca (1930–1977), a veteran of the Stan Kenton and Woody Herman bands, and baritone saxophonist, composer and arranger Bill Holman. They co-led a 1957 octet session for HiFi Records.

Talking Heads.name: Talking Heads
Talking Heads.summary: New York new wave band formed in 1975 by David Byrne, Chris Frantz, Tina Weymouth and later Jerry Harrison. They grew out of the CBGB scene and blended art rock with funk and world-music rhythms, releasing eight studio albums before breaking up in 1991; they entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2002.

studio_albums.title: More Songs About Buildings and Food

Peter Brown.name: Peter Brown
Peter Brown.summary: American singer, songwriter and producer from Illinois who scored late-1970s disco hits with Do Ya Wanna Get Funky with Me and Dance with Me. He later co-wrote Madonna's Material Girl, stepped away from music in the late 1980s, and returned with a new album in 2018.

Lyrics Born.name: Lyrics Born
Lyrics Born.summary: Tokyo-born, Bay Area-raised rapper, singer and producer Tom Shimura, known for his rapid, funk-driven delivery. He is half of the duo Latyrx with Lateef the Truthspeaker and a member of the Quannum collective, and has released solo albums since 2003.

Superstar Quamallah.name: Superstar Quamallah
Superstar Quamallah.summary: Brooklyn-born rapper, DJ and producer who worked in the Bay Area and Los Angeles underground hip-hop scenes, collaborating with figures linked to Hieroglyphics and the Likwit Crew. The son of organist Big John Patton, he later taught hip-hop studies at UC Berkeley; his jazz-rap album Invisible Man appeared around 2009.

Aretha Franklin.name: Aretha Franklin
Aretha Franklin.summary: Aretha Franklin (1942–2018), raised in Detroit and trained in her father's church, became the defining soul singer of the late 1960s after joining Atlantic Records, earning the nickname Queen of Soul. Her hits include Respect and Natural Woman, and she won 18 Grammy Awards across a six-decade career.

studio_albums.title: The Tender, the Moving, the Swinging Aretha Franklin

I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You
Take It Like You Give It
This Girl's in Love with You
Hey Now Hey (The Other Side of the Sky)
With Everything I Feel in Me
What You See Is What You Sweat
A Rose Is Still a Rose
Aretha: A Woman Falling Out of Love
Aretha Franklin Sings the Great Diva Classics

Tower of Power.name: Tower of Power
Tower of Power.summary: Oakland, California, soul and funk band formed in 1968 by saxophonists Emilio Castillo and Stephen Kupka, famous for its tight horn section. Hits include So Very Hard to Go and You're Still a Young Man, and their horns have appeared on many other artists' recordings.

Chic.name: Chic
Chic.summary: New York band founded in the 1970s by guitarist Nile Rodgers and bassist Bernard Edwards, whose sleek disco-funk sound produced hits such as Le Freak and Good Times. The duo also wrote and produced for other artists, and Rodgers has continued to lead the group since Edwards died in 1996.

Amii Stewart.name: Amii Stewart
Amii Stewart.summary: American singer, dancer and actress from Washington, D.C., who reached No. 1 in the US in 1979 with a disco version of Knock on Wood. She later settled in Italy, where she built a long career recording pop, jazz and film-music projects and appearing on stage and television.

studio_albums.title: Pearls – Amii Stewart Sings Ennio Morricone

Village People.name: Village People
Village People.summary: Disco group assembled in 1977 by French producers Jacques Morali and Henri Belolo with lead singer Victor Willis, whose members dressed as costumed American archetypes. They scored worldwide hits such as Y.M.C.A., Macho Man, In the Navy and Go West.

Millie Jackson.name: Millie Jackson
Millie Jackson.summary: Soul and R&B singer born in Thomson, Georgia, in 1944, famous for frank, often humorous spoken monologues woven into her songs. Her 1974 album Caught Up established that style, and she recorded prolifically into the 1990s, with several gold albums.

studio_albums.title: I Got to Try It One Time

Tony Mottola.name: Tony Mottola
Tony Mottola.summary: New Jersey guitarist Tony Mottola (1918–2004) was a busy New York session and radio player, a member of the Tonight Show orchestra from 1958 to 1972, and a frequent accompanist to Frank Sinatra in the 1980s. He recorded dozens of easy-listening guitar albums for Command and Project 3.

studio_albums.title: Two Guitars for Two in Love
Tony Mottola and the Quad Guitars
Tony Mottola and the Brass Menagerie
I Only Have Eyes for You

Nina Simone.name: Nina Simone
Nina Simone.summary: Nina Simone (1933–2003), born Eunice Waymon in North Carolina, was a classically trained pianist who became a singer blending jazz, blues, gospel and folk. In the 1960s she became a prominent voice of the civil rights movement with songs like Mississippi Goddam, and she later lived largely in Europe.

studio_albums.title: I Put a Spell on You

Peter Frampton.name: Peter Frampton
Peter Frampton.summary: English guitarist and singer who came to prominence with The Herd and Humble Pie before going solo in 1972. His live double album Frampton Comes Alive! made him a superstar in 1976, and he is known for his talk-box guitar sound; he joined the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2024.

studio_albums.title: Hummingbird in a Box: Songs for a Ballet

Sarah Webster Fabio.name: Sarah Webster Fabio
Sarah Webster Fabio.summary: Nashville-born poet, critic and teacher (1928–1979) active in the Black Arts Movement and in establishing Black studies programs in California. She taught at Merritt College and UC Berkeley and recorded several albums of her poetry for Folkways, some set to music performed by her children.

studio_albums.title: Boss Soul: 12 Poems by Sarah Webster Fabio
Soul Ain't, Soul Is: Poems by Sarah Webster Fabio
Jujus / Alchemy of the Blues: Poems by Sarah Webster Fabio

Donald Byrd.name: Donald Byrd
Donald Byrd.summary: Detroit-born jazz trumpeter Donald Byrd (1932–2013) emerged as a leading hard bop player in the 1950s, recording extensively for Blue Note. In the 1970s he moved into jazz-funk and soul, scoring a commercial breakthrough with Black Byrd, and he also had a long career as a music educator.

studio_albums.title: Thank You...For F.U.M.L. (Funking Up My Life)
New Formulas from the Jazz Lab

Alfred Hitchcock.name: Alfred Hitchcock
Alfred Hitchcock.summary: The English-born film director, celebrated as a master of suspense, also lent his voice and name to a few novelty records tied to his television series. These included a 1958 mood-music LP with Jeff Alexander's orchestra and a 1962 collection of ghost stories for children.

studio_albums.title: Alfred Hitchcock Presents Music to Be Murdered By
Alfred Hitchcock Presents Ghost Stories for Young People

Mary Poppins Original Cast.name: Mary Poppins Original Cast
Mary Poppins Original Cast.summary: The performers of Disney's 1964 musical film, led by Julie Andrews and Dick Van Dyke, recorded the Sherman Brothers songs for the film's soundtrack. That cast recording topped the US album chart and won Grammy Awards.

Sharon Jones & The Dap Kings.name: Sharon Jones & The Dap Kings
Sharon Jones & The Dap Kings.summary: A Brooklyn soul and funk band fronted by singer Sharon Jones and closely tied to Daptone Records, at the heart of the 2000s retro-soul revival. The Dap-Kings also backed Amy Winehouse; Jones died of pancreatic cancer in 2016.

studio_albums.title: Dap Dippin' with Sharon Jones and the Dap-Kings
Give the People What They Want

Miles Davis.name: Miles Davis
Miles Davis.summary: An American trumpeter, bandleader and composer (1926-1991) who shaped several eras of jazz, from bebop and cool jazz through modal jazz to jazz fusion. His recordings, including Kind of Blue and Bitches Brew, rank among the most influential in the genre.

studio_albums.title: Miles: The New Miles Davis Quintet

The Moody Blues.name: The Moody Blues
The Moody Blues.summary: An English rock band formed in Birmingham in 1964 that began in R&B before pioneering orchestral, concept-driven progressive rock with Days of Future Passed. Known for Nights in White Satin, they were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2018.

studio_albums.title: In Search of the Lost Chord
On the Threshold of a Dream

Frances Faye.name: Frances Faye
Frances Faye.summary: An American cabaret singer and pianist from Brooklyn (1912-1991), known for energetic nightclub shows full of risque wordplay and altered lyrics. She recorded for labels such as Capitol, Bethlehem, Imperial and Verve and appeared in the 1978 film Pretty Baby.

studio_albums.title: Swinging All the Way with Frances Faye

The xx.name: The xx
The xx.summary: An English indie band formed in 2005 in Wandsworth, London, made up of Romy Madley Croft, Oliver Sim and producer Jamie xx. Their sparse, intimate sound won the 2010 Mercury Prize for their debut album.

John Lennon.name: John Lennon
John Lennon.summary: An English singer-songwriter (1940-1980) who co-founded the Beatles and later pursued a solo career, often working with his wife Yoko Ono. His solo work includes Imagine and Double Fantasy; he was shot and killed in New York in 1980.

studio_albums.title: Unfinished Music No. 2: Life with the Lions
Some Time in New York City

Townes Van Zandt.name: Townes Van Zandt
Townes Van Zandt.summary: A Texas-born singer-songwriter (1944-1997) admired for bleak, poetic lyrics and fingerpicked guitar. Though he sold modestly himself, his songs Pancho and Lefty and If I Needed You became country hits for Willie Nelson with Merle Haggard and for Emmylou Harris with Don Williams.

studio_albums.title: For the Sake of the Song
The Late Great Townes Van Zandt

Billie Holiday.name: Billie Holiday
Billie Holiday.summary: An American jazz singer (1915-1959) whose phrasing and emotional delivery made her one of the most influential vocalists of the century. Known as Lady Day, she recorded Strange Fruit and many standards, and cut her later LPs mostly for Norman Granz's labels.

studio_albums.title: Music for Torching with Billie Holiday

Marlena Shaw.name: Marlena Shaw
Marlena Shaw.summary: An American singer and pianist from New Rochelle, New York, who worked across jazz, soul and R&B for labels including Cadet, Blue Note and Columbia. Her recordings such as California Soul have been widely sampled; she died in 2024.

studio_albums.title: From the Depths of My Soul

Pablo Cruise.name: Pablo Cruise
Pablo Cruise.summary: A soft rock band formed in San Francisco in 1973 that blended pop, rock and jazz influences. They had their biggest successes in the late 1970s with hits such as Whatcha Gonna Do? and Love Will Find a Way.

The Rolling Stones.name: The Rolling Stones
The Rolling Stones.summary: The Rolling Stones are an English rock band formed in London in 1962, long anchored by Mick Jagger and Keith Richards. Rooted in blues and rock and roll, they have released music and toured for more than six decades and are among the most commercially successful acts in history.

Neil Diamond.name: Neil Diamond
Neil Diamond.summary: Neil Diamond is an American singer-songwriter from Brooklyn who began as a Brill Building-era songwriter before becoming one of the best-selling pop artists of his time. His many hits include Sweet Caroline, Cracklin' Rosie and Song Sung Blue, and he retired from touring in 2018 after a Parkinson's diagnosis.

studio_albums.title: I'm Glad You're Here with Me Tonight
On the Way to the Sky
The Best Years of Our Lives
Up on the Roof: Songs from the Brill Building
The Movie Album: As Time Goes By

Joni Mitchell.name: Joni Mitchell
Joni Mitchell.summary: A Canadian singer-songwriter and painter born in 1943 who emerged from the late-1960s folk scene and later explored jazz and pop. Records such as Blue and Court and Spark made her one of the most admired songwriters of her generation.

studio_albums.title: Chalk Mark in a Rain Storm

Fleetwood Mac.name: Fleetwood Mac
Fleetwood Mac.summary: A British-American rock band founded in London in 1967 as a blues group led by Peter Green. After Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks joined in 1975 they became a pop-rock powerhouse, with Rumours ranking among the best-selling albums ever made.

World Class Wreckin Cru.name: World Class Wreckin Cru
World Class Wreckin Cru.summary: An electro and hip hop group from the Los Angeles area built around DJ Alonzo Williams and his Eve After Dark nightclub. Dr. Dre and DJ Yella were members before going on to form N.W.A. The group was active mainly in the mid-1980s, with a brief return around 1990.

Bukue One.name: Bukue One
Bukue One.summary: A San Francisco Bay Area rapper, born Tion Torrence, who is also a skateboarder, graffiti artist and music manager. He founded Urban Productions in 1998 and worked with acts such as Blackalicious, Aceyalone and Del the Funky Homosapien before releasing his own full-length debut in 2007.

People Under The Stairs.name: People Under The Stairs
People Under The Stairs.summary: A Los Angeles hip hop duo of Thes One and Double K, formed in 1997 and known for sample-heavy, self-produced records. They released a dozen albums on labels including Om Records before ending the group in 2019; Double K died in 2021.

studio_albums.title: Question in the Form of an Answer

Damu The Fudgemunk.name: Damu The Fudgemunk
Damu The Fudgemunk.summary: The stage name of Earl Davis, a Washington, D.C. hip hop producer, DJ and multi-instrumentalist born in 1984. He is known for jazz-tinged instrumental beat records on Redefinition and Def Presse and for frequent collaborations with rappers such as Raw Poetic, Flex Mathews and Blu.

studio_albums.title: How It Should Sound Vol. 3, 4, and 5

N.W.A..name: N.W.A.
N.W.A..summary: A hip hop group from Compton, California, formed in 1987 with Eazy-E, Dr. Dre, Ice Cube, MC Ren, DJ Yella and Arabian Prince. Its explicit, confrontational records helped define gangsta rap and drew wide controversy. The group split in 1991 and entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2016.

Joe Cocker.name: Joe Cocker
Joe Cocker.summary: An English rock and soul singer from Sheffield, active from the 1960s until his death in 2014, known for his gravelly voice and intense stage presence. He rose to fame with a reworked Beatles cover and a celebrated Woodstock set, and later scored hits including a Grammy-winning duet.

studio_albums.title: With a Little Help from My Friends
I Can Stand a Little Rain

Deep Sea Diver.name: Deep Sea Diver
Deep Sea Diver.summary: A Seattle indie rock band that began in 2007 as the project of singer and guitarist Jessica Dobson. The lineup has included drummer Peter Mansen, and the group has released records on labels such as High Beam and Sub Pop.

Spirit.name: Spirit
Spirit.summary: A Los Angeles rock band formed in 1967 that mixed psychedelic rock with jazz and blues influences. Its core included guitarist Randy California and his stepfather, drummer Ed Cassidy. The band peaked commercially around 1968 to 1970 and effectively ended with California's death in 1997.

studio_albums.title: The Adventures of Kaptain Kopter & Commander Cassidy in Potato Land

The Doobie Brothers.name: The Doobie Brothers
The Doobie Brothers.summary: A California rock band formed in San Jose in 1970, first fronted by Tom Johnston with a guitar-driven sound. After Michael McDonald joined in the mid-1970s they moved toward soft rock and soul, scoring major hits before breaking up in 1982 and later reuniting.

studio_albums.title: What Were Once Vices Are Now Habits

Billy Joel.name: Billy Joel
Billy Joel.summary: An American singer, songwriter and pianist from New York, often called the Piano Man after his breakthrough song. He was one of the top-selling artists of the 1970s and 1980s, and after 1993 he largely stopped making pop albums while continuing to tour.

Malo.name: Malo
Malo.summary: A Latin rock band from San Francisco formed around 1971, led by Arcelio Garcia and guitarist Jorge Santana, younger brother of Carlos Santana. Blending Latin percussion with rock, jazz and blues, the group is best known for its 1972 hit Suavecito.

Linda Ronstadt.name: Linda Ronstadt
Linda Ronstadt.summary: An American singer from Tucson, Arizona, who moved from the folk-rock Stone Poneys to a hugely successful solo career. She recorded across country rock, pop, standards and Mexican traditional music, won multiple Grammys, and retired from singing after Parkinson's-related illness.

studio_albums.title: Linda Ronstadt, Stone Poneys and Friends, Vol. III
Cry Like a Rainstorm, Howl Like the Wind
Dedicated to the One I Love

Bob Moses.name: Bob Moses
Bob Moses.summary: An electronic music duo of Vancouver natives Tom Howie and Jimmy Vallance, who formed the act in New York City. Their music mixes deep house with indie rock songwriting, and a remix of their song Tearing Me Up won a Grammy for best remixed recording.

Sly & The Family Stone.name: Sly & The Family Stone
Sly & The Family Stone.summary: A San Francisco band led by Sly Stone, formed in 1966 with a racially integrated, mixed-gender lineup. Fusing soul, rock and psychedelia, it was central to the rise of funk, with hits such as Everyday People and the landmark album There's a Riot Goin' On.

studio_albums.title: Heard Ya Missed Me, Well I'm Back

J.J. Johnson & Kai Winding.name: J.J. Johnson & Kai Winding
J.J. Johnson & Kai Winding.summary: A jazz partnership between trombonists J. J. Johnson and Kai Winding, who co-led a popular two-trombone group starting in 1954 and reunited on later records. Their tight, arranged bebop style produced several albums for Savoy, Bethlehem, Columbia and Impulse. Johnson was the more prolific leader overall.

studio_albums.title: J. J. Johnson with Sonny Stitt
Jay Jay Johnson with Clifford Brown
Jazz Workshop, Volume One: Trombone Rapport
The Eminent Jay Jay Johnson, Vol. 2
Jazz Workshop, Volume Two: Trombone Rapport
The Eminent Jay Jay Johnson, Vol. 3
The Eminent Jay Jay Johnson, Vol. 1
André Previn and J. J. Johnson
Things Are Getting Better All the Time

Maynard Ferguson.name: Maynard Ferguson
Maynard Ferguson.summary: Canadian-born jazz trumpeter and bandleader (1928-2006) famed for his extreme upper-register playing. After featuring with Stan Kenton, he led big bands from the 1950s onward and reached a pop audience in the 1970s with his recording of Gonna Fly Now from Rocky.

studio_albums.title: Around the Horn with Maynard Ferguson

Johnny Richards And His Orchestra.name: Johnny Richards And His Orchestra
Johnny Richards And His Orchestra.summary: The recording orchestra of Johnny Richards (1911-1968), a Mexican-born American arranger, composer and conductor. He wrote extensively for Stan Kenton, including Cuban Fire!, composed the tune of Young at Heart, and led his own big bands on record from the mid-1950s.

Bob Scobey's Frisco Band.name: Bob Scobey's Frisco Band
Bob Scobey's Frisco Band.summary: Traditional jazz ensemble formed around 1949 by trumpeter Bob Scobey (1916-1963), a veteran of Lu Watters' Yerba Buena Jazz Band. Based in the San Francisco area, it recorded heavily for Good Time Jazz and featured banjoist and vocalist Clancy Hayes.

Caterina Valente.name: Caterina Valente
Caterina Valente.summary: Paris-born singer, guitarist, dancer and actress of Italian parentage (1931-2024) who built an international career from the 1950s. Fluent in several languages and able to sing in many more, she was especially popular in Germany and the US, retiring from performing in 2003.

Prince.name: Prince
Prince.summary: Prince (1958–2016) was an American singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist from Minneapolis who often played every instrument on his records. Blending funk, rock, R&B and pop, he achieved huge success with Purple Rain and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2004.

studio_albums.title: Around the World in a Day

Bobby Hackett.name: Bobby Hackett
Bobby Hackett.summary: American jazz cornetist, trumpeter and guitarist from Providence, Rhode Island (1915-1976). Known for his warm, lyrical tone, he worked with Glenn Miller and Benny Goodman and was the featured soloist on Jackie Gleason's popular mood-music albums.

Barbra Streisand.name: Barbra Streisand
Barbra Streisand.summary: Barbra Streisand is an American singer, actress and director born in Brooklyn in 1942. Since her 1963 debut album she has become one of the best-selling recording artists of all time, and she has won Academy, Emmy, Grammy and Tony honors.

studio_albums.title: The Secret of Life: Partners, Volume Two

Sarah Vaughan.name: Sarah Vaughan
Sarah Vaughan.summary: American jazz vocalist from Newark, New Jersey (1924-1990), nicknamed Sassy and The Divine One. Admired for her wide range and harmonic sophistication, she emerged in the bebop era and recorded prolifically for labels including Mercury, EmArcy, Roulette and Pablo.

Nancy Wilson.name: Nancy Wilson
Nancy Wilson.summary: American singer from Ohio (1937-2018) whose work spanned jazz, pop and R&B. Signed to Capitol in 1960, she released dozens of albums, won multiple Grammy Awards, and also hosted her own television program and a long-running public radio show.

studio_albums.title: Can't Take My Eyes Off You

The Police.name: The Police
The Police.summary: English rock trio formed in London in 1977 by Sting, Stewart Copeland and Andy Summers. Mixing new wave, punk and reggae, they released five albums before splitting in the mid-1980s, later reuniting for a world tour in 2007-2008.

Adele.name: Adele
Adele.summary: English singer-songwriter from London, born in 1988, whose albums are named after her age at the time of writing. Known for soulful ballads, she has sold well over a hundred million records and won numerous Grammy Awards.

Joan Armatrading.name: Joan Armatrading
Joan Armatrading.summary: British singer-songwriter and guitarist born in 1950 on Saint Kitts and raised in Birmingham, England. Active since the early 1970s, she is known for songs like Love and Affection and has earned Grammy and Ivor Novello nominations.

studio_albums.title: How Did This Happen and What Does It Now Mean

The Pretenders.name: The Pretenders
The Pretenders.summary: The Pretenders are a rock band formed in 1978 in England by American singer and guitarist Chrissie Hynde with James Honeyman-Scott, Pete Farndon and Martin Chambers. After early new wave success, the lineup changed often, with Hynde remaining the constant through decades of releases.

Tears For Fears.name: Tears For Fears
Tears For Fears.summary: English pop and new wave duo from Bath founded in 1981 by Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith. They had major 1980s hits including Shout and Everybody Wants to Rule the World, and returned with new material in the 2020s.

studio_albums.title: Raoul and the Kings of Spain

Prince And The Revolution.name: Prince And The Revolution
Prince And The Revolution.summary: Billing used for Prince together with his Minneapolis backing band the Revolution, whose members included Wendy Melvoin, Lisa Coleman and Bobby Z. The collaboration produced Purple Rain, Around the World in a Day and Parade before Prince disbanded the group in 1986.

studio_albums.title: Around the World in a Day

Traffic.name: Traffic
Traffic.summary: Traffic was an English rock band formed in 1967 around Steve Winwood, Jim Capaldi, Chris Wood and Dave Mason. Mixing psychedelia, folk, jazz and blues, they released a string of albums through 1974, briefly reunited in 1994, and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2004.

studio_albums.title: The Low Spark of High Heeled Boys
Shoot Out at the Fantasy Factory

Bikini Kill.name: Bikini Kill
Bikini Kill.summary: Bikini Kill is a punk band formed in Olympia, Washington, in 1990, fronted by Kathleen Hanna with Tobi Vail, Kathi Wilcox and Billy Karren. Recording mainly for Kill Rock Stars, they became central figures of the riot grrrl movement before splitting in 1997, later reuniting for tours.

Bratmobile.name: Bratmobile
Bratmobile.summary: Bratmobile is a punk band founded in Olympia, Washington, in 1991 by Allison Wolfe, Molly Neuman and later Erin Smith. One of the earliest riot grrrl groups, they split onstage in 1994, regrouped in 1999 for two more albums, and have reunited occasionally since.

Red Hot Chili Peppers.name: Red Hot Chili Peppers
Red Hot Chili Peppers.summary: Red Hot Chili Peppers are an American rock band formed in Los Angeles in 1983, built around singer Anthony Kiedis and bassist Flea. Fusing funk, punk and alternative rock, they rank among the best-selling bands ever and entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2012.

Sir Sly.name: Sir Sly
Sir Sly.summary: Sir Sly is an American indie pop trio from Southern California made up of singer Landon Jacobs with Jason Suwito and Hayden Coplen. Active since 2012, they reached alternative radio with songs such as Gold, You Haunt Me and &Run.

Frank Ocean.name: Frank Ocean
Frank Ocean.summary: Frank Ocean is an American singer and songwriter raised in New Orleans who moved to Los Angeles after Hurricane Katrina and joined the Odd Future collective. After the mixtape Nostalgia, Ultra, he released the acclaimed albums Channel Orange and Blonde.

The George Benson Quartet.name: The George Benson Quartet
The George Benson Quartet.summary: The George Benson Quartet was the small soul-jazz group that guitarist George Benson led in the mid-1960s, featuring organist Lonnie Smith and baritone saxophonist Ronnie Cuber. Benson, born in Pittsburgh in 1943, later became a major pop and jazz star with Breezin' and has won ten Grammys.

Kay Starr.name: Kay Starr
Kay Starr.summary: Kay Starr was an American singer born in Oklahoma in 1922 who worked across pop, jazz and country. She is best remembered for the chart-topping Wheel of Fortune in 1952 and recorded mainly for Capitol and RCA Victor; she died in 2016.

studio_albums.title: The One, The Only Kay Starr
When the Lights Go on Again

Herb Alpert's Tijuana Brass.name: Herb Alpert's Tijuana Brass
Herb Alpert's Tijuana Brass.summary: Herb Alpert's Tijuana Brass began in 1962 as trumpeter Herb Alpert overdubbing his own horn, launching A&M Records with Jerry Moss. The group's Latin-flavored pop instrumentals sold enormously in the mid-1960s; Alpert disbanded it in 1969 and has revived the name at times since.

Bee Gees.name: Bee Gees
Bee Gees.summary: The Bee Gees were a vocal group of brothers Barry, Robin and Maurice Gibb, who began in Australia in the late 1950s. Known for tight harmonies, they had pop hits in the 1960s and dominated the disco era with Saturday Night Fever, becoming one of the best-selling acts ever.

Morris Jefferson.name: Morris Jefferson
Morris Jefferson.summary: Morris Jefferson is a Chicago-born disco and funk performer. His single Spank Your Blank Blank charted on the US R&B list in 1978, and he released a second album in 1984 before turning to gospel music in later years.

Arctic Monkeys.name: Arctic Monkeys
Arctic Monkeys.summary: Arctic Monkeys are a rock band from Sheffield, England, formed in 2002 and fronted by Alex Turner. Their 2006 debut became the fastest-selling first album in UK chart history, and every album since has topped the British chart.

studio_albums.title: Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not

The Books.name: The Books
The Books.summary: The Books were an American duo of guitarist Nick Zammuto and cellist Paul de Jong, formed in New York around 2000. They built intricate songs from acoustic instruments and collaged found recordings, releasing four albums before splitting in 2012.

Dean Martin.name: Dean Martin
Dean Martin.summary: Dean Martin (1917–1995) was an American crooner, actor and comedian who first gained fame in a comedy partnership with Jerry Lewis. As a solo singer on Capitol and later Reprise he scored hits such as Everybody Loves Somebody, and he hosted a long-running NBC variety show.

Frank Sinatra.name: Frank Sinatra
Frank Sinatra.summary: Frank Sinatra (1915–1998) was an American singer and actor from Hoboken, New Jersey, who rose with the big bands of Harry James and Tommy Dorsey. Babatunde Olatunji.name: Babatunde Olatunji
Babatunde Olatunji.summary: Babatunde Olatunji (1927–2003) was a Nigerian percussionist, teacher and activist who came to the United States to study at Morehouse College. His 1959 Columbia album Drums of Passion helped introduce African drumming to American listeners, and he later worked with John Coltrane, Mickey Hart and others.

Men At Work.name: Men At Work
Men At Work.summary: Men at Work are an Australian rock band formed in Melbourne in 1979 and fronted by Colin Hay. Their debut album and the songs Who Can It Be Now? and Down Under topped charts in Australia, the US and the UK, and they won the 1983 Grammy for Best New Artist.

Cecilio & Kapono.name: Cecilio & Kapono
Cecilio & Kapono.summary: Cecilio & Kapono are a Honolulu duo of Cecilio Rodriguez and Henry Kapono Ka'aihue, active in the 1970s and again in the 1990s. Their albums blend soft rock and pop with soul, funk and Hawaiian influences, beginning with three releases on Columbia.

Simon And Garfunkel.name: Simon And Garfunkel
Simon And Garfunkel.summary: Simon & Garfunkel were the New York folk rock duo of Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel, who grew up together in Queens. Their harmonies carried hits such as The Sound of Silence, Mrs. Robinson and Bridge over Troubled Water before they split in 1970, with occasional later reunions.

A Flock Of Seagulls.name: A Flock Of Seagulls
A Flock Of Seagulls.summary: A Flock of Seagulls are a new wave band from Liverpool formed in 1979 around singer Mike Score. They found international success in the early 1980s, notably with I Ran (So Far Away), and won a Grammy for the instrumental D.N.A.

studio_albums.title: The Story of a Young Heart
The Light at the End of the World

Kajagoogoo.name: Kajagoogoo
Kajagoogoo.summary: Kajagoogoo are an English new wave band from Leighton Buzzard who adopted the name in 1982 with Limahl as singer. Their debut single Too Shy topped the UK chart in 1983; after Limahl left, bassist Nick Beggs took over vocals, and the group briefly renamed itself Kaja before splitting.

Bing Crosby & Rosemary Clooney.name: Bing Crosby & Rosemary Clooney
Bing Crosby & Rosemary Clooney.summary: A duet pairing of Bing Crosby (1903–1977), one of the best-selling singers and film stars of the twentieth century, and Rosemary Clooney (1928–2002), a popular vocalist of the 1950s. The two co-starred in the film White Christmas and recorded duet albums, including Fancy Meeting You Here in 1958.

Willie Nelson & Ray Price.name: Willie Nelson & Ray Price
Willie Nelson & Ray Price.summary: A joint billing of country singers Willie Nelson and Ray Price, who had worked together since Nelson played bass in Price's band in the early 1960s. They recorded several duet albums, starting with San Antonio Rose in 1980. Nelson, born in Texas in 1933, became a leading figure of the outlaw country movement.

Judy Garland.name: Judy Garland
Judy Garland.summary: Judy Garland (1922–1969) was an American singer and actress who became a star at MGM, most famously as Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz. Her later career included acclaimed concert work, and her 1961 album Judy at Carnegie Hall won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

Chicago.name: Chicago
Chicago.summary: Chicago is an American rock band with a horn section, founded in Chicago in 1967 and first known as the Chicago Transit Authority. Mixing rock with jazz, R&B and pop, it has sold well over 100 million records and is among the most commercially successful American groups.

studio_albums.title: Chicago XXXVIII: Born for This Moment

Bob Dylan.name: Bob Dylan
Bob Dylan.summary: Bob Dylan is an American singer-songwriter who emerged from the early 1960s folk scene and later embraced electric rock, country and gospel. Regarded as one of the most influential songwriters in popular music, he received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016.

studio_albums.title: Good as I Been to You

Leon Bridges.name: Leon Bridges
Leon Bridges.summary: Leon Bridges, born Todd Michael Bridges in Atlanta and raised in Fort Worth, Texas, is an American soul and R&B singer known for a sound rooted in 1960s soul. He won a Grammy for Best Traditional R&B Performance and has also recorded collaborative releases with Khruangbin.

Jefferson Starship.name: Jefferson Starship
Jefferson Starship.summary: Jefferson Starship is a San Francisco rock band launched in 1974 by former Jefferson Airplane members Paul Kantner and Grace Slick. It peaked commercially with the chart-topping Red Octopus, evolved into Starship after Kantner left in 1984, and was later revived by Kantner in 1992.

Led Zeppelin.name: Led Zeppelin
Led Zeppelin.summary: Led Zeppelin was an English rock band formed in London in 1968 by Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, John Paul Jones and John Bonham. Blending blues, folk and heavy riffs, they became one of the best-selling acts ever and disbanded in 1980 after Bonham died.

Tame Impala.name: Tame Impala
Tame Impala.summary: Tame Impala is the psychedelic music project of Australian multi-instrumentalist Kevin Parker, begun in Perth in 2007. Parker writes, plays, records and produces the studio material himself, while a touring band performs live; the project has won several ARIA and J Awards.

Daft Punk.name: Daft Punk
Daft Punk.summary: Daft Punk was a French electronic duo of Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, formed in Paris in 1993. Known for their robot personas and influence on house and dance music, they won multiple Grammys before announcing their split in 2021.

The Ventures.name: The Ventures
The Ventures.summary: The Ventures are an American instrumental rock group founded in Tacoma, Washington, in 1958 by Don Wilson and Bob Bogle. Famed for Walk, Don't Run and the Hawaii Five-O theme, they shaped surf guitar music, enjoyed huge popularity in Japan and entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

Keely Smith.name: Keely Smith
Keely Smith.summary: Keely Smith was an American jazz and pop singer who rose to fame in the 1950s performing and recording with bandleader Louis Prima, her husband at the time. Pink Floyd.name: Pink Floyd
Pink Floyd.summary: Pink Floyd were an English rock band formed in London in 1965, pioneers of psychedelic and progressive rock noted for conceptual albums and elaborate stage shows. With Syd Barrett, Roger Waters, David Gilmour, Richard Wright and Nick Mason, they became one of the best-selling acts in history.

studio_albums.title: The Piper at the Gates of Dawn
The Dark Side of the Moon

Mitski.name: Mitski
Mitski.summary: Mitski, born Mitsuki Laycock in Japan in 1990 and based in New York, is a singer-songwriter working in indie rock and art pop. She released her first albums while studying music at Purchase College, and Be the Cowboy brought her wide indie success.

studio_albums.title: Retired from Sad, New Career in Business
The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We
Nothing's About to Happen to Me

Orion Sun.name: Orion Sun
Orion Sun.summary: Orion Sun is the stage name of Tiffany Majette, an American singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and producer from Mount Laurel, New Jersey. Signed to Mom + Pop, she works across alternative R&B and indie styles and released her debut album in 2020.

Vikki Carr.name: Vikki Carr
Vikki Carr.summary: Vikki Carr is an American singer born in El Paso, Texas, in 1940 to Mexican parents. She scored an international pop hit with It Must Be Him in 1967 and later found her greatest success with Spanish-language albums, winning several Grammy Awards.
