Terry Snyder And The All Stars.name: Terry Snyder And The All Stars
Terry Snyder And The All Stars.summary: Terry Snyder and the All Stars was a credit used by Command Records for studio musicians led by drummer Terry Snyder under producer Enoch Light. Their stereo percussion showcase records, starting with Persuasive Percussion, were major sellers in the early hi-fi era.

LCD Soundsystem.name: LCD Soundsystem
LCD Soundsystem.summary: American dance-punk and electronic rock group formed in Brooklyn by producer James Murphy, co-founder of DFA Records. The band split in 2011 after a farewell concert at Madison Square Garden and reunited in 2015.

Harry Belafonte.name: Harry Belafonte
Harry Belafonte.summary: American singer, actor and civil rights activist born in New York to Caribbean parents, who popularized calypso music in the 1950s. His album Calypso was among the first LPs to sell over a million copies. He died in 2023.

The Maytones.name: The Maytones
The Maytones.summary: Jamaican reggae vocal duo of Vernon Buckley and Gladstone Grant, named after their hometown of May Pen in Clarendon. Active from the late 1960s until 1980, they moved from rocksteady to roots reggae and scored with the song Madness, later reuniting in the 2000s.

Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin & Sammy Davis.name: Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin & Sammy Davis Jr.
Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin & Sammy Davis.summary: Joint billing of three entertainers at the core of the so-called Rat Pack, who shared stages in Las Vegas, especially at the Sands Hotel, in the early 1960s and also appeared in films together. Their shows mixed standards with improvised comedy.

Queen.name: Queen
Queen.summary: British rock band formed in London in 1970 by Freddie Mercury, Brian May, Roger Taylor and John Deacon. Known for theatrical live shows and genre-spanning songs such as Bohemian Rhapsody, they rank among the best-selling acts in music history.

Fleet Foxes.name: Fleet Foxes
Fleet Foxes.summary: Indie folk band from Seattle led by singer-songwriter Robin Pecknold, formed in 2006. The group is known for close vocal harmonies and pastoral arrangements and records for Sub Pop and later Anti-.

Journey.name: Journey
Journey.summary: American rock band formed in San Francisco in 1973 by former Santana members including Neal Schon. After Steve Perry joined as singer in 1977 they became one of the most commercially successful arena rock acts, known for songs like Don't Stop Believin'.

Beyoncé.name: Beyoncé
Beyoncé.summary: American singer, songwriter and performer from Houston who first rose to fame with Destiny's Child before a hugely successful solo career. She holds the record for the most Grammy Awards won by any artist.

Melanie.name: Melanie
Melanie.summary: American singer-songwriter Melanie Safka, who performed at Woodstock in 1969 and had hits such as Lay Down (Candles in the Rain) and Brand New Key. She recorded prolifically for decades and died in 2024.

Beach House.name: Beach House
Beach House.summary: Dream pop duo from Baltimore consisting of singer and keyboardist Victoria Legrand and guitarist Alex Scally, formed in 2004. They are known for hazy, slow-building songs with organ and reverb-heavy guitar.

Buena Vista Social Club.name: Buena Vista Social Club
Buena Vista Social Club.summary: Ensemble of veteran Cuban musicians brought together in Havana in 1996 to record traditional son and related styles, named after a former members' club. Their album and the Wim Wenders documentary about them sparked worldwide interest in Cuban music.

TV On The Radio.name: TV On The Radio
TV On The Radio.summary: Experimental rock band formed in Brooklyn in 2001 by Tunde Adebimpe and David Andrew Sitek, later joined by Kyp Malone and others. They blend post-punk, soul, electronic and art rock elements.

The Chemical Brothers.name: The Chemical Brothers
The Chemical Brothers.summary: English electronic music duo of Tom Rowlands and Ed Simons, formed in Manchester in 1989. They were pioneers of the big beat style and have won several Grammy Awards for their dance records.

The Shins.name: The Shins
The Shins.summary: American indie rock band formed in Albuquerque in 1996 and led by singer-songwriter James Mercer, later based in Portland, Oregon. Their melodic pop songs gained a wide audience in the 2000s.

Dawn Richard.name: Dawn Richard
Dawn Richard.summary: American singer, songwriter and producer from New Orleans who first gained attention in the group Danity Kane and later in Diddy – Dirty Money. Her solo work blends electronic music and R&B.

Portugal. The Man.name: Portugal. The Man
Portugal. The Man.summary: American rock band formed in Wasilla, Alaska, in 2004 and later based in Portland, Oregon, fronted by John Gourley. After years of independent and major-label releases, they reached mainstream success with the 2017 single Feel It Still.

Paul Simon.name: Paul Simon
Paul Simon.summary: American singer-songwriter from New Jersey who first found fame in the duo Simon & Garfunkel before a long solo career. His solo work, including Graceland, has drawn on many world music traditions and earned numerous Grammy Awards.

King Curtis.name: King Curtis
King Curtis.summary: American saxophonist, bandleader and session player born Curtis Ousley, active in rhythm and blues, jazz and rock and roll. He scored with Soul Twist and Soul Serenade and served as Aretha Franklin's musical director before being fatally stabbed in New York in 1971.

Radiohead.name: Radiohead
Radiohead.summary: English rock band formed in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, in 1985, led by singer Thom Yorke. Moving from guitar rock to electronic and experimental styles, they became one of the most acclaimed and influential bands of their era.

Diana Krall.name: Diana Krall
Diana Krall.summary: Canadian jazz pianist and singer from Nanaimo, British Columbia, known for her smoky contralto and interpretations of standards. She has sold millions of records and won multiple Grammy and Juno Awards.

Lizzo.name: Lizzo
Lizzo.summary: Lizzo, born Melissa Viviane Jefferson, is an American singer, rapper and flautist who began her career in Minneapolis. Her blend of pop, R&B and hip hop brought major success from 2019, along with several Grammy Awards.

Round Robin And Brimstone.name: Round Robin And Brimstone
Round Robin And Brimstone.summary: Soul and boogie group led by Robin Lloyd, who also headed The Round Robin Monopoly. Their lone self-titled LP became a rare collector item and was reissued by Luv N' Haight in 2021.

The Match.name: The Match
The Match.summary: American vocal pop group that recorded the album A New Light for RCA Victor in Hollywood in 1969, performing sunshine pop and soft rock versions of contemporary songs.

Lauer.name: Lauer
Lauer.summary: Lauer is the alias of Phillip Lauer, a German producer and DJ from Frankfurt whose music mixes deep house with synth-pop and Italo-disco. He is also half of Tuff City Kids with Gerd Janson and works with Fabrizio Mammarella as Black Spuma.

Country Joe & The Fish.name: Country Joe & The Fish
Country Joe & The Fish.summary: Psychedelic rock band formed in Berkeley, California, in 1965 around Country Joe McDonald and Barry Melton. Known for anti-war songs such as the Fixin'-to-Die Rag, they performed at Monterey Pop and Woodstock.

studio_albums.title: Electric Music for the Mind and Body

Ella Fitzgerald.name: Ella Fitzgerald
Ella Fitzgerald.summary: American jazz vocalist often called the First Lady of Song, admired for her pure tone, precise diction and scat improvisation. Over a career of nearly six decades she recorded extensively, notably her Song Book series, and won 13 Grammy Awards.

Nice Work If You Can Get It

Crosby, Stills & Nash.name: Crosby, Stills & Nash
Crosby, Stills & Nash.summary: Folk rock supergroup of David Crosby, Stephen Stills and Graham Nash, formed in 1968 from members of the Byrds, Buffalo Springfield and the Hollies. Renowned for vocal harmonies, they also recorded and toured with Neil Young as CSNY and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

Cream.name: Cream
Cream.summary: British rock trio of Eric Clapton, Jack Bruce and Ginger Baker, active from 1966 to 1968. Often described as an early supergroup, they fused blues, psychedelia and hard rock with long improvised live jams and sold millions of records before splitting.

The Who.name: The Who
The Who.summary: English rock band formed in London in 1964, classically Roger Daltrey, Pete Townshend, John Entwistle and Keith Moon. Famous for explosive concerts and rock operas such as Tommy and Quadrophenia, they are among the most influential rock acts of their era.

The Dave Brubeck Quartet.name: The Dave Brubeck Quartet
The Dave Brubeck Quartet.summary: Jazz group led by pianist Dave Brubeck from 1951, best known for the lineup with Paul Desmond, Eugene Wright and Joe Morello. They popularized jazz on college campuses and had a crossover hit with Time Out, which explored unusual time signatures.

studio_albums.title: Anything Goes! The Dave Brubeck Quartet Plays Cole Porter

!!!.summary: American dance-punk band, pronounced chk chk chk, formed in Sacramento in 1996 and led by singer Nic Offer. Mixing punk energy with disco, funk and house, they have released most of their albums on Warp Records.

Kool & The Gang.name: Kool & The Gang
Kool & The Gang.summary: American band founded in Jersey City in 1964 by brothers Robert Kool Bell and Ronald Bell. They moved from jazz-funk to polished pop-R&B, scoring hits such as Jungle Boogie, Celebration and Get Down On It.

Marvin Gaye.name: Marvin Gaye
Marvin Gaye.summary: American soul singer, songwriter and producer who became a leading Motown artist in the 1960s with hits and duets with Tammi Terrell. His later self-directed albums, including What's Going On and Let's Get It On, reshaped soul music before his death in 1984.

studio_albums.title: The Soulful Moods of Marvin Gaye
How Sweet It Is to Be Loved by You
A Tribute to the Great Nat "King" Cole

Westside Strutters.name: Westside Strutters
Westside Strutters.summary: One-off disco studio project assembled in 1979 to record Gershwin '79, a set of dance arrangements of George and Ira Gershwin songs. Produced by drummer Ross Salomone, it drew on Los Angeles session musicians and singers.

Cleo Sol.name: Cleo Sol
Cleo Sol.summary: English singer-songwriter from Ladbroke Grove, London, working in soul and alternative R&B. She is the lead voice of the collective SAULT, has appeared on Little Simz tracks, and makes her solo records with her husband, producer Inflo.

Gorillaz.name: Gorillaz
Gorillaz.summary: A British virtual band created in 1998 by Damon Albarn and artist Jamie Hewlett, presented through four cartoon members. Their music combines alternative rock, hip hop and electronic styles with many guest collaborators, and they have sold tens of millions of records.

studio_albums.title: Song Machine, Season One: Strange Timez

Black Pumas.name: Black Pumas
Black Pumas.summary: A psychedelic soul act from Austin, Texas, formed in 2018 by singer Eric Burton and guitarist-producer Adrian Quesada. Their debut album earned several Grammy nominations, including Album of the Year and Best New Artist.

Bad Religion.name: Bad Religion
Bad Religion.summary: A Los Angeles punk rock band formed in 1980, fronted by Greg Graffin with guitarist Brett Gurewitz, whose Epitaph label releases much of their work. They are known for melodic hardcore with dense vocal harmonies and politically and intellectually minded lyrics.

studio_albums.title: How Could Hell Be Any Worse?

Butts Band.name: Butts Band
Butts Band.summary: A rock group formed in 1973 by Robby Krieger and John Densmore after the Doors ended, first with singer Jess Roden. It released two albums with completely different lineups before breaking up in 1975.

The Fugees.name: The Fugees
The Fugees.summary: A hip hop trio from New Jersey made up of Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and Pras Michel. Their second album, The Score, became one of the best-selling hip hop records ever before the members split to pursue solo careers.

Paul McCartney & Wings.name: Paul McCartney & Wings
Paul McCartney & Wings.summary: Wings was the band Paul McCartney formed in 1971 with his wife Linda and guitarist Denny Laine, and several releases were credited to Paul McCartney and Wings. The group had numerous hits through the 1970s before disbanding in 1981.

studio_albums.title: Wings at the Speed of Sound

Breakestra.name: Breakestra
Breakestra.summary: A Los Angeles funk ensemble started in 1997 by Miles Tackett that performs live versions of classic funk and soul breaks often sampled in hip hop. After two Live Mix releases it moved on to albums of original material.

Daryl Hall & John Oates.name: Daryl Hall & John Oates
Daryl Hall & John Oates.summary: Philadelphia duo of singer Daryl Hall and guitarist John Oates, blending rock, soul and pop. They scored six US number one singles, mostly in the late 1970s and early 1980s, and rank among the best-selling duos in music history.

Mongo Santamaria.name: Mongo Santamaria
Mongo Santamaria.summary: Havana-born conga player and bandleader who worked with Tito Puente and Cal Tjader before leading his own groups from the late 1950s. He wrote Afro Blue and had a 1963 pop hit with Herbie Hancock's Watermelon Man.

Cowboy Junkies.name: Cowboy Junkies
Cowboy Junkies.summary: A Toronto band formed in 1985 by siblings Margo, Michael and Peter Timmins with bassist Alan Anton. Their slow, hushed blend of alternative country, folk and blues found wide attention with The Trinity Session in 1988.

studio_albums.title: At the End of Paths Taken

Commodores.name: Commodores
Commodores.summary: A funk and soul band formed in Tuskegee, Alabama, that signed to Motown in the early 1970s. With Lionel Richie as a key singer and writer they had hits such as Brick House, Easy and Three Times a Lady, and continued after he left in 1982.

Buddy Guy.name: Buddy Guy
Buddy Guy.summary: Louisiana-born guitarist and singer who became a central figure of Chicago blues, serving as a Chess Records session player in the 1960s. After a quieter 1980s he enjoyed a major revival, winning several Grammys, and entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2005.

studio_albums.title: Left My Blues in San Francisco
Damn Right, I've Got the Blues
The Blues Is Alive and Well

Grateful Dead.name: Grateful Dead
Grateful Dead.summary: A rock band founded in 1965 in the San Francisco Bay Area, led by Jerry Garcia. Famous for long improvised concerts that mixed rock, folk, blues, country and jazz, they built a devoted touring following until Garcia's death in 1995.

The B-52's.name: The B-52's
The B-52's.summary: A new wave band formed in Athens, Georgia, in 1976, known for retro kitsch styling, beehive hairdos and playful dance songs. After an early cult following, they reached their commercial peak with Cosmic Thing and the hit Love Shack.

Isaac Hayes.name: Isaac Hayes
Isaac Hayes.summary: Memphis soul singer, songwriter and producer who first wrote hits for Sam and Dave at Stax with David Porter. His extended orchestral soul albums and the Shaft theme, which won an Academy Award, made him a star; he later voiced Chef on South Park.

The Doors.name: The Doors
The Doors.summary: Los Angeles rock band formed in 1965 by singer Jim Morrison, keyboardist Ray Manzarek, guitarist Robby Krieger and drummer John Densmore. Known for hits like Light My Fire and for Morrison's poetic, provocative stage persona, they continued briefly as a trio after his death in 1971.

The 5th Dimension.name: The 5th Dimension
The 5th Dimension.summary: American vocal group from Los Angeles that blended pop, soul and Broadway influences. Working largely with producer Bones Howe, they scored late-1960s and early-1970s hits such as Up, Up and Away, Stoned Soul Picnic and Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In.

The Beat.name: The Beat
The Beat.summary: Power pop and new wave band from Los Angeles led by singer-songwriter Paul Collins, formerly of the Nerves. Formed in 1977, the group recorded for Columbia and has continued in various lineups, sometimes billed as the Paul Collins Beat.

Michael Jackson.name: Michael Jackson
Michael Jackson.summary: American singer, songwriter and dancer who rose to fame as a child with the Jackson 5 and became one of the most commercially successful entertainers ever. Often called the King of Pop, he released landmark albums including Off the Wall, Thriller and Bad before his death in 2009.

studio_albums.title: HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I

The Humblebums.name: The Humblebums
The Humblebums.summary: Folk group from Glasgow active from 1965 to 1971, whose members included Billy Connolly, Tam Harvey and Gerry Rafferty. After the group broke up, Connolly turned to comedy and Rafferty went on to a successful solo career.

Frankie Goes To Hollywood.name: Frankie Goes To Hollywood
Frankie Goes To Hollywood.summary: Liverpool pop band fronted by Holly Johnson that rose to fame in 1984 on the ZTT label with producer Trevor Horn. Their first three singles, Relax, Two Tribes and The Power of Love, all topped the UK chart, but the group split after a second album.

Baby Grand.name: Baby Grand
Baby Grand.summary: Philadelphia rock band of the late 1970s that included Rob Hyman and Eric Bazilian, who later founded the Hooters. Produced by Rick Chertoff, they released two albums on Arista before disbanding.

The Miracles.name: The Miracles
The Miracles.summary: Detroit vocal group formed in the 1950s and led by Smokey Robinson, one of the first acts signed to Motown. They had many 1960s hits, then continued with Billy Griffin as lead singer after Robinson left in 1972, scoring a number one with Love Machine.

studio_albums.title: Time Out for Smokey Robinson & The Miracles

Kleeer.name: Kleeer
Kleeer.summary: Funk, disco and post-disco band from New York City active from 1972 to 1985 and signed to Atlantic Records. Members included Richard Lee, Norman Durham, Paul Crutchfield and Woody Cunningham.

Patti Smith Group.name: Patti Smith Group
Patti Smith Group.summary: The backing band of New York singer and poet Patti Smith, with guitarist Lenny Kaye among its members, credited on her late-1970s albums. Smith herself is a key figure of the punk era whose debut Horses was a landmark; the studio list below is her full discography.

Billie Holiday & Al Hibbler.name: Billie Holiday & Al Hibbler
Billie Holiday & Al Hibbler.summary: A joint billing pairing two separate singers on one record: jazz vocalist Billie Holiday and baritone Al Hibbler, a former Duke Ellington band singer known for Unchained Melody. They did not work as a duo; their earlier recordings were combined on a 1968 Sunset LP.

Poco.name: Poco
Poco.summary: Country rock band formed in Los Angeles in 1968 by Richie Furay and Jim Messina after Buffalo Springfield broke up. Through many lineup changes the group helped shape the genre, with its biggest chart success coming with Legend in 1978.

Arrow.name: Arrow
Arrow.summary: Stage name of Alphonsus Cassell (1949-2010), a calypso and soca performer from Montserrat. His 1982 song Hot Hot Hot became an international hit and is often called the best-selling soca record ever.

Al Stewart.name: Al Stewart
Al Stewart.summary: Scottish-born singer-songwriter who emerged from the British folk scene of the 1960s and became known for songs drawing on historical subjects. His greatest success came with the albums Year of the Cat and Time Passages in the late 1970s.

Grand Funk Railroad.name: Grand Funk Railroad
Grand Funk Railroad.summary: Hard rock band from Flint, Michigan, formed in 1969 by Mark Farner, Don Brewer and Mel Schacher, later adding keyboardist Craig Frost. A major concert draw in the 1970s, they topped the singles chart with We're an American Band and The Loco-Motion.

studio_albums.title: All the Girls in the World Beware!!!

Gladys Knight & The Pips.name: Gladys Knight & The Pips
Gladys Knight & The Pips.summary: Family R&B and soul vocal group from Atlanta, fronted by Gladys Knight with her brother Bubba and cousins. They recorded for Motown and later Buddah, scoring hits such as I Heard It Through the Grapevine and Midnight Train to Georgia, and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

Modern English.name: Modern English
Modern English.summary: New wave and post-punk band from Colchester, England, formed in 1979 around singer Robbie Grey and signed to 4AD in 1980. They are best known for I Melt with You from After the Snow, and Grey has led later reunions of the group.

The Kinks.name: The Kinks
The Kinks.summary: English rock band from north London led by brothers Ray and Dave Davies, active from 1963 until 1996. Early hits like You Really Got Me helped shape hard rock, while Ray Davies's later songwriting explored English life and theatrical concept albums.

studio_albums.title: The Kinks Are the Village Green Preservation Society
Arthur (Or the Decline and Fall of the British Empire)
Lola Versus Powerman and the Moneygoround, Part One
Give the People What They Want

Gerry Cinnamon.name: Gerry Cinnamon
Gerry Cinnamon.summary: Scottish singer-songwriter born Gerard Crosbie in 1984 and raised in Castlemilk, Glasgow, playing acoustic indie folk. He built a large following while unsigned, topped the UK chart with The Bonny on his own label, and sold out multiple nights at Hampden Park in 2022.

Bob Marley & The Wailers.name: Bob Marley & The Wailers
Bob Marley & The Wailers.summary: Jamaican reggae group formed in the 1960s by Bob Marley, Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer, later led by Marley alone with an expanded band and the I Threes. Their Island Records albums of the 1970s carried reggae and Rastafarian themes to audiences around the world.

Foo Fighters.name: Foo Fighters
Foo Fighters.summary: American rock band started in Seattle in 1994 by former Nirvana drummer Dave Grohl, who recorded the first album largely alone before forming a full lineup. They became one of the most commercially successful rock acts of their era and have won numerous Grammy Awards.

studio_albums.title: There Is Nothing Left to Lose

The Velvet Underground & Nico.name: The Velvet Underground & Nico
The Velvet Underground & Nico.summary: Billing for the 1967 pairing of New York rock band the Velvet Underground, led by Lou Reed and John Cale, with German singer and model Nico, brought together under Andy Warhol's patronage. Nico sang on three songs of their debut before departing; the band continued without her.

Eddie Money.name: Eddie Money
Eddie Money.summary: American rock singer born Edward Mahoney in Manhattan in 1949, who left police training to pursue music in Berkeley. He had hits including Baby Hold On, Two Tickets to Paradise and Take Me Home Tonight, and died in 2019.

Wet Willie.name: Wet Willie
Wet Willie.summary: Southern rock band from Mobile, Alabama, fronted by singer Jimmy Hall, that moved to Macon and recorded for Capricorn before switching to Epic. Their biggest hit was Keep On Smilin' in 1974, followed by later chart singles such as Street Corner Serenade and Weekend.

Franke & The Knockouts.name: Franke & The Knockouts
Franke & The Knockouts.summary: Pop rock band from New Brunswick, New Jersey, led by singer-songwriter Franke Previte and active from 1980 to 1986. Their single Sweetheart reached the US top ten in 1981, and later drummer Tico Torres went on to join Bon Jovi.

John Williams.name: John Williams
John Williams.summary: American composer and conductor born in 1932, renowned for film scores including Jaws, Star Wars, E.T. and the Indiana Jones and Harry Potter films. He also led the Boston Pops Orchestra and has received many Academy Award nominations and wins.

Wallace Davenport.name: Wallace Davenport
Wallace Davenport.summary: New Orleans jazz trumpeter (1925-2004) who moved between traditional jazz, swing and bebop. He worked with Lionel Hampton, Count Basie, Ray Charles and Lloyd Price, and from 1971 issued recordings of his own groups on his My Jazz label.

Bob James.name: Bob James
Bob James.summary: American jazz keyboardist, arranger and producer born in Missouri in 1939, a key figure in smooth jazz and fusion. He worked as an arranger at CTI, founded the Tappan Zee label, wrote the Taxi theme Angela, and co-founded the group Fourplay.

studio_albums.title: The Genie: Themes & Variations from the TV Series "Taxi"
Once Upon a Time: The Lost 1965 New York Studio Sessions

The Jimi Hendrix Experience.name: The Jimi Hendrix Experience
The Jimi Hendrix Experience.summary: Rock trio formed in London in 1966 with guitarist Jimi Hendrix, bassist Noel Redding and drummer Mitch Mitchell. Over three albums they redefined electric guitar playing, and the group was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1992.

Al Green.name: Al Green
Al Green.summary: American soul singer from Arkansas who, with producer Willie Mitchell at Hi Records, made a string of early 1970s hits such as Let's Stay Together. He later became a pastor in Memphis and turned largely to gospel music, winning multiple Grammys.

studio_albums.title: Al Green Gets Next to You
I'm Still in Love with You
The Lord Will Make a Way

Curtis Mayfield.name: Curtis Mayfield
Curtis Mayfield.summary: Chicago soul singer, guitarist and producer who first found fame leading the Impressions before going solo in 1970 and founding the Curtom label. His socially conscious songwriting and the Super Fly soundtrack made him a major influence; he died in 1999.

studio_albums.title: There's No Place Like America Today
We Come in Peace with a Message of Love

The Toys.name: The Toys
The Toys.summary: Female vocal trio from Jamaica, Queens, made up of Barbara Harris, Barbara Parritt and June Montiero, active through the mid-1960s. Their 1965 single A Lover's Concerto, based on a Bach minuet, reached No. 2 in the US and sold over two million copies.

studio_albums.title: The Toys Sing "A Lover's Concerto" and "Attack!"

Simple Minds.name: Simple Minds
Simple Minds.summary: A rock band from Glasgow led by singer Jim Kerr and guitarist Charlie Burchill. Starting in the late 1970s new wave scene, they became an arena act in the mid-1980s with hits such as Don't You (Forget About Me) and Alive and Kicking.

studio_albums.title: Good News from the Next World

The National.name: The National
The National.summary: An American indie rock band formed in Cincinnati and based in Brooklyn, fronted by Matt Berninger with two pairs of brothers, the Dessners and the Devendorfs. They rose to wide acclaim in the late 2000s and 2010s.

The Clash.name: The Clash
The Clash.summary: A London punk band formed in 1976 around Joe Strummer and Mick Jones. They broadened punk with reggae, dub, rockabilly and other influences and remained active until the mid-1980s.

David Bowie.name: David Bowie
David Bowie.summary: An English singer, songwriter and actor whose career spanned five decades, from the late 1960s until his death in 2016. He was known for constant stylistic reinvention and stage personas such as Ziggy Stardust.

studio_albums.title: The Man Who Sold the World
The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars

The Fatback Band.name: The Fatback Band
The Fatback Band.summary: A funk and disco group founded in New York City in 1970 by drummer Bill Curtis, later known simply as Fatback. They scored R&B hits such as I Like Girls and are often credited with one of the first commercially issued rap singles, King Tim III.

Lenny White.name: Lenny White
Lenny White.summary: An American jazz fusion drummer born in Queens in 1949, best known as a member of Chick Corea's Return to Forever. He also played on Miles Davis's Bitches Brew, has led his own groups and worked as a producer.

studio_albums.title: The Love Has Never Gone: Tribute to Earth, Wind & Fire

Duran Duran.name: Duran Duran
Duran Duran.summary: A new wave and synth-pop band formed in Birmingham, England, in 1978. They were among the leading acts of the early MTV era, with hits such as Hungry Like the Wolf, Rio and The Reflex.

Tom Jones.name: Tom Jones
Tom Jones.summary: A Welsh singer whose powerful voice brought him fame from the mid-1960s with songs like It's Not Unusual and Delilah. He has recorded across pop, soul, country and gospel over a career lasting more than six decades.

studio_albums.title: The Body and Soul of Tom Jones
Memories Don't Leave Like People Do
Don't Let Our Love Get Lonely
Things That Matter Most to Me
The Lead and How to Swing It

Taj Mahal.name: Taj Mahal
Taj Mahal.summary: An American blues musician, born Henry St. Claire Fredericks, who plays guitar, piano, harmonica and banjo. Since the late 1960s he has blended blues with Caribbean, African, Hawaiian and other world music traditions.

studio_albums.title: Giant Step/De Ole Folks at Home
Happy Just to Be Like I Am
Mkutano Meets the Culture Musical Club of Zanzibar

The Brian Jonestown Massacre.name: The Brian Jonestown Massacre
The Brian Jonestown Massacre.summary: A psychedelic rock band from San Francisco led by Anton Newcombe, known for a prolific output and frequent lineup changes. The group was a central subject of the 2004 documentary Dig!.

Bob Welch.name: Bob Welch
Bob Welch.summary: An American guitarist and singer-songwriter who belonged to Fleetwood Mac from 1971 to 1974. He later had solo success in the late 1970s with songs such as Sentimental Lady, and he died in 2012.

studio_albums.title: His Fleetwood Mac Years and Beyond, Vol. 2
Sings the Best Songs Ever Written

Dave Mason.name: Dave Mason
Dave Mason.summary: An English singer, guitarist and songwriter who co-founded Traffic in 1967 and wrote Feelin' Alright. He went on to a long solo career, scoring a hit with We Just Disagree, and played on records by many major artists before his death in 2026.

studio_albums.title: Old Crest on a New Wave

The Sweet.name: The Sweet
The Sweet.summary: A British glam rock band formed in London in the late 1960s. They scored many hits in the 1970s, including Block Buster!, The Ballroom Blitz and Fox on the Run, and later moved toward a heavier rock sound.

studio_albums.title: Funny How Sweet Co-Co Can Be

Pearl Jam.name: Pearl Jam
Pearl Jam.summary: A rock band formed in Seattle in 1990, fronted by Eddie Vedder, and one of the leading groups of the grunge era. Their debut Ten made them stars, and they have continued recording and touring for decades.

John Coltrane.name: John Coltrane
John Coltrane.summary: An American jazz saxophonist and composer active from the 1940s until his death in 1967. He moved from hard bop through modal jazz to free jazz and recorded landmark works such as Giant Steps and A Love Supreme.

studio_albums.title: John Coltrane with the Red Garland Trio
Both Directions at Once: The Lost Album

The New Ventures.name: The New Ventures
The New Ventures.summary: A billing used by the American instrumental rock group the Ventures for the album Rocky Road, released by United Artists in 1976.

Afu-Ra.name: Afu-Ra
Afu-Ra.summary: A rapper from Brooklyn, New York, linked with the Gang Starr Foundation and collaborators such as DJ Premier and Jeru the Damaja. His lyrics often draw on martial arts and spiritual themes.

The Strokes.name: The Strokes
The Strokes.summary: The Strokes are a New York rock band formed in 1998, with Julian Casablancas, Nick Valensi, Albert Hammond Jr., Nikolai Fraiture and Fabrizio Moretti. Their 2001 debut helped spark the garage rock revival of the early 2000s.

INXS.name: INXS
INXS.summary: INXS were an Australian rock group formed in Sydney in 1977, fronted by Michael Hutchence until his death in 1997. Mixing new wave, funk and pop rock, they reached global fame with the 1987 album Kick.

Curtis Amy & Dupree Bolton.name: Curtis Amy & Dupree Bolton
Curtis Amy & Dupree Bolton.summary: This billing pairs Texas-born saxophonist Curtis Amy (1929-2002), a fixture of the early 1960s Los Angeles jazz scene who later did extensive studio work, with the gifted but rarely recorded trumpeter Dupree Bolton. The two co-led the 1963 Pacific Jazz session Katanga!

The Call.name: The Call
The Call.summary: The Call were an American rock band formed in Santa Cruz, California, in 1980 and led by singer Michael Been. Known for I Still Believe and the rock chart-topper Let the Day Begin, they split in 2000 and later regrouped to finish archival recordings.

Gerry Rafferty.name: Gerry Rafferty
Gerry Rafferty.summary: Gerry Rafferty (1947-2011) was a Scottish singer-songwriter who first worked with the Humblebums and Stealers Wheel. His solo career peaked with the 1978 album City to City and its saxophone-driven hit Baker Street.

studio_albums.title: Can I Have My Money Back?
On a Wing and a Prayer

The Jimmy Castor Bunch.name: The Jimmy Castor Bunch
The Jimmy Castor Bunch.summary: The Jimmy Castor Bunch was the funk and soul group led by New York saxophonist and singer Jimmy Castor (1940-2012). Their biggest success came in 1972 with Troglodyte (Cave Man), and tracks like It's Just Begun became heavily sampled in hip-hop.

studio_albums.title: The Jimmy Castor Bunch Featuring the Everything Man

Hot Chocolate.name: Hot Chocolate
Hot Chocolate.summary: Hot Chocolate were a British soul and pop band formed in London in 1968 and fronted by singer Errol Brown. Working mostly with producer Mickie Most on RAK, they scored many hits, including You Sexy Thing and the chart-topper So You Win Again.

Lionel Richie.name: Lionel Richie
Lionel Richie.summary: Lionel Richie, born in 1949 in Tuskegee, Alabama, rose to fame as a singer and writer with the Commodores before going solo in 1982. He became one of the leading ballad singers of the 1980s with hits such as Truly, All Night Long and Hello.

Jimmy Cliff.name: Jimmy Cliff
Jimmy Cliff.summary: Jimmy Cliff, born James Chambers in Jamaica in 1948, is a reggae singer and actor who starred in the film The Harder They Come. His well-known songs include Many Rivers to Cross, You Can Get It If You Really Want and a 1993 hit cover of I Can See Clearly Now.

studio_albums.title: Give the People What They Want

Lou Rawls.name: Lou Rawls
Lou Rawls.summary: Lou Rawls (1933-2006) was a Chicago-born soul, jazz and blues singer who began in gospel with the Pilgrim Travelers. He enjoyed hits on Capitol in the 1960s and later on Philadelphia International, notably You'll Never Find Another Love Like Mine, and won several Grammy Awards.

Reverend Gary Davis.name: Reverend Gary Davis
Reverend Gary Davis.summary: Reverend Gary Davis (1896-1972) was a blind South Carolina-born guitarist and Baptist minister who played gospel, blues and ragtime with an intricate two-finger picking style. Rediscovered in the 1960s folk revival, he taught and influenced many players, including Dave Van Ronk and Bob Weir.

studio_albums.title: The Guitar & Banjo of Reverend Gary Davis

Sex Pistols.name: Sex Pistols
Sex Pistols.summary: The Sex Pistols were a London punk band formed in 1975 and managed by Malcolm McLaren, featuring Johnny Rotten, Steve Jones, Paul Cook and Glen Matlock, later replaced by Sid Vicious. Though active only briefly before splitting in 1978, they had an enormous cultural impact.

studio_albums.title: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols

John Mayall.name: John Mayall
John Mayall.summary: John Mayall (1933-2024) was an English blues singer and multi-instrumentalist whose Bluesbreakers served as a training ground for Eric Clapton, Peter Green and Mick Taylor. He later settled in Los Angeles, recorded prolifically for decades and was appointed OBE in 2005.

studio_albums.title: New Year, New Band, New Company
In the Palace of the King

Parliament.name: Parliament
Parliament.summary: Parliament is an American funk band George Clinton built in the late 1960s out of the New Jersey doo-wop group the Parliaments. As the flagship of his P-Funk collective, it toured alongside Funkadelic and produced theatrical, sci-fi themed records through the 1970s.

The Peace.name: The Peace
The Peace.summary: The Peace were a Zamrock band from Kitwe, Zambia, active in the early to mid 1970s and led in their final form by guitarist Teddy Makombe. They split in 1976 after making a second album that was never released and is now lost.

Champaign.name: Champaign
Champaign.summary: R&B and soul band named after its hometown of Champaign, Illinois. They scored a transatlantic hit in 1981 with How 'Bout Us and later had R&B successes such as Try Again, reforming in later decades to record new albums.

Against All Logic.name: Against All Logic
Against All Logic.summary: Pseudonym of Chilean American electronic producer Nicolás Jaar, used for house-oriented and sample-heavy dance music. Under the name he released singles and an EP in the mid-2010s, followed by the albums 2012–2017 and 2017–2019.

Silver Convention.name: Silver Convention
Silver Convention.summary: German Euro disco act created in Munich by producers Michael Kunze and Sylvester Levay, later fronted by a female vocal trio. Their instrumental Fly, Robin, Fly topped the US chart and won a Grammy, and they represented Germany at Eurovision in 1977.

War.name: War
War.summary: Funk and soul band from Long Beach, California, which began in 1969 backing Eric Burdon before working on its own. Their blend of funk, Latin and rock produced hits including Spill the Wine, The Cisco Kid and Low Rider.

The Band.name: The Band
The Band.summary: Canadian-American roots rock group that started as the Hawks behind Ronnie Hawkins and later backed Bob Dylan. They became known for songs like The Weight, bid farewell with The Last Waltz in 1976, and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

Pet Shop Boys.name: Pet Shop Boys
Pet Shop Boys.summary: English electronic pop duo of singer Neil Tennant and keyboardist Chris Lowe, formed in London in 1981. They broke through with West End Girls and became one of the most commercially successful duos in UK chart history.

John Lennon & Yoko Ono.name: John Lennon & Yoko Ono
John Lennon & Yoko Ono.summary: Joint billing of former Beatle John Lennon and his wife, artist Yoko Ono, who recorded together from the late 1960s. Their shared releases include Some Time in New York City, Double Fantasy, which won Album of the Year, and the posthumous Milk and Honey.

studio_albums.title: Some Time in New York City

Ike & Tina Turner.name: Ike & Tina Turner
Ike & Tina Turner.summary: Husband-and-wife R&B and soul duo of Ike Turner and Tina Turner, active from 1960 to 1976 with their touring revue. Their hits included River Deep – Mountain High, Proud Mary and Nutbush City Limits, and they entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1991.

studio_albums.title: The Soul of Ike & Tina Turner
Ike & Tina Turner's Kings of Rhythm Dance
The Gospel According to Ike & Tina

Bob Geldof.name: Bob Geldof
Bob Geldof.summary: Irish singer and activist who led the Boomtown Rats before going solo in the mid-1980s. He co-organised Band Aid and Live Aid to raise money for famine relief, and has released several solo albums since 1986.

studio_albums.title: Deep in the Heart of Nowhere
How to Compose Popular Songs That Will Sell

U.K..name: U.K.
U.K..summary: British progressive rock supergroup formed in 1977 by John Wetton, Eddie Jobson, Allan Holdsworth and Bill Bruford. After the first album it continued as a trio with drummer Terry Bozzio, split in 1980, and later reunited for tours in the 2010s.

Run-D.M.C..name: Run-D.M.C.
Run-D.M.C..summary: Hip hop trio from Hollis, Queens, made up of Joseph Simmons, Darryl McDaniels and Jason Mizell. They helped bring rap into the mainstream in the 1980s, notably by pairing with Aerosmith on Walk This Way.

Jane's Addiction.name: Jane's Addiction
Jane's Addiction.summary: Alternative rock band formed in Los Angeles in 1985 and fronted by Perry Farrell. They were influential in the late 1980s alternative scene, and Farrell launched the Lollapalooza festival as their farewell tour in 1991.

The Pasadenas.name: The Pasadenas
The Pasadenas.summary: English R&B and pop vocal group signed to Columbia, active from 1988 until 2005. They had eight UK top 40 singles, including Tribute (Right On) and their biggest hit, a 1992 cover of I'm Doing Fine Now.

The Daptone Super Soul Revue.name: The Daptone Super Soul Revue
The Daptone Super Soul Revue.summary: A touring showcase of acts from the Brooklyn soul and funk label Daptone Records. Its December 2014 run at the Apollo Theater featured Sharon Jones and the Dap-Kings, Charles Bradley, Antibalas, the Budos Band and others, and was released as a live album in 2021.

Donny Hathaway.name: Donny Hathaway
Donny Hathaway.summary: Chicago-born soul, R&B and gospel singer, songwriter and keyboardist (1945-1979). He is remembered for The Ghetto, This Christmas and his celebrated duets with Roberta Flack, and received a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award.

Diana Ross.name: Diana Ross
Diana Ross.summary: American singer and actress who rose to fame as lead vocalist of the Supremes before launching a solo career at Motown in 1970. Her solo catalogue spans more than two dozen studio albums, including the Chic-produced Diana.

studio_albums.title: Why Do Fools Fall in Love
Every Day Is a New Day
Diana Ross Sings Songs from The Wiz

Van Morrison.name: Van Morrison
Van Morrison.summary: Belfast-born singer-songwriter, born 1945, who first fronted the R&B group Them before a long solo career. His music blends soul, jazz, folk and Celtic elements, and he has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and knighted.

studio_albums.title: His Band and the Street Choir
No Guru, No Method, No Teacher
How Long Has This Been Going On
Tell Me Something: The Songs of Mose Allison
Born to Sing: No Plan B

The Ahmad Jamal Trio.name: The Ahmad Jamal Trio
The Ahmad Jamal Trio.summary: The piano trio led by American jazz pianist Ahmad Jamal (1930-2023), born Frederick Russell Jones in Pittsburgh. His 1958 live set At the Pershing: But Not for Me was a major commercial success and influenced Miles Davis, and he was later named an NEA Jazz Master.

studio_albums.title: Listen to the Ahmad Jamal Quintet
The Bright, the Blue and the Beautiful
Ahmad Jamal with The Assai Quartet
Saturday Morning: La Buissonne Studio Sessions

Glen Hansard.name: Glen Hansard
Glen Hansard.summary: Irish singer-songwriter from Dublin, born 1970, who leads the rock band the Frames and formed the Swell Season with Marketa Irglova. He starred in the film Once and shared the Academy Award for Best Original Song for Falling Slowly.

studio_albums.title: All That Was East Is West of Me Now

Betty Davis.name: Betty Davis
Betty Davis.summary: American funk and soul singer and songwriter from North Carolina, born in 1945, who was briefly married to Miles Davis in the late 1960s. She released a handful of bold, sexually frank funk albums in the mid-1970s before withdrawing from music.

Digital Underground.name: Digital Underground
Digital Underground.summary: Hip-hop group from Oakland, California, founded in the late 1980s by Shock G with Chopmaster J and Kenny-K. Known for P-Funk-inspired humour and the hit The Humpty Dance, the group also helped launch Tupac Shakur's career.

Madonna.name: Madonna
Madonna.summary: American singer, songwriter and performer who emerged from the New York club scene in the early 1980s. Frequently reinventing her image and sound, she became one of the best-selling recording artists in history, with albums such as True Blue and Ray of Light.

Family.name: Family
Family.summary: English progressive rock band from Leicester, active from the late 1960s until 1973 and fronted by singer Roger Chapman. Their eclectic blend of rock, folk and jazz earned a strong UK following, though they made little impact in America.

Rush.name: Rush
Rush.summary: Canadian rock trio formed in Toronto in 1968, best known for the line-up of Geddy Lee, Alex Lifeson and Neil Peart. Famed for technically ambitious progressive and hard rock, they released nineteen studio albums before Peart's retirement and death in 2020 ended the band's run.

The Daktaris.name: The Daktaris
The Daktaris.summary: A Brooklyn funk and Afrobeat studio project whose name, Swahili for doctors, nods to the TV series Daktari. Featuring Cameroonian drummer Jojo Kuo and players who later joined the Dap-Kings and Antibalas, it drew on 1970s African musicians such as Fela Kuti and released one album.

Donald Byrd & Gigi Gryce.name: Donald Byrd & Gigi Gryce
Donald Byrd & Gigi Gryce.summary: A late-1950s partnership between trumpeter Donald Byrd (1932-2013) and alto saxophonist Gigi Gryce, who co-led the Jazz Lab group and several albums together. Byrd later moved from hard bop into jazz-funk, mentored Herbie Hancock, and became an NEA Jazz Master.

studio_albums.title: Thank You...For F.U.M.L. (Funking Up My Life)

Jimi Hendrix.name: Jimi Hendrix
Jimi Hendrix.summary: An American guitarist and singer who released three studio albums during his lifetime between 1967 and 1968. After his death in September 1970, many further studio albums were assembled from his unfinished recordings, starting with The Cry of Love in 1971.

studio_albums.title: First Rays of the New Rising Sun

Khruangbin.name: Khruangbin
Khruangbin.summary: A Houston trio formed in 2010 by bassist Laura Lee Ochoa, guitarist Mark Speer and drummer Donald Johnson. Their largely instrumental music mixes Thai rock, Iranian pop and dub with American soul and psychedelia, and is often tagged as Thai funk.

studio_albums.title: The Universe Smiles Upon You II

Michelle Shocked.name: Michelle Shocked
Michelle Shocked.summary: An American singer-songwriter born Karen Michelle Johnston in Dallas in 1962. A field recording from the 1986 Kerrville Folk Festival led to a Mercury deal and three albums there, after which she released music independently on her own labels.

Bruce Springsteen.name: Bruce Springsteen
Bruce Springsteen.summary: American singer-songwriter from New Jersey, often backed by the E Street Band, known for heartland rock songs about working-class American life. Albums such as Born to Run and Born in the U.S.A. made him one of the best-selling and most honoured rock performers.

studio_albums.title: The Wild, the Innocent & the E Street Shuffle
Darkness on the Edge of Town
We Shall Overcome: The Seeger Sessions

Dadawah.name: Dadawah
Dadawah.summary: A one-off recording name used by Jamaican Rastafarian musician Ras Michael, also known for leading the Sons of Negus. Its sole album, released in 1974, joins Nyahbinghi drumming with dub production in a devotional style.

Impact All Stars.name: Impact All Stars
Impact All Stars.summary: A Jamaican studio band name credited on instrumental and dub records issued on the Impact! label in the 1970s. Their releases include Java Java Java Java and Randy's Dub, later reissued by 17 North Parade and VP Records.

Lou Donaldson.name: Lou Donaldson
Lou Donaldson.summary: An American jazz alto saxophonist who led around fifty albums between 1953 and 2000 for labels such as Blue Note and Argo. His output spans hard bop and the soul jazz and funk styles he favoured from the 1960s onward.

studio_albums.title: New Faces New Sounds (Lou Donaldson Quintet/Quartet)
New Faces New Sounds (Lou Donaldson / Clifford Brown Quintet)
Color as a Way of Life

System Of A Down.name: System Of A Down
System Of A Down.summary: An Armenian-American heavy metal band formed in Glendale, California, in 1994, featuring Serj Tankian, Daron Malakian, Shavo Odadjian and John Dolmayan. They have sold over 40 million records, had three albums debut at number one in the US, and won a Grammy for B.Y.O.B.

The Kingstonians.name: The Kingstonians
The Kingstonians.summary: A rocksteady and reggae vocal trio from Kingston, Jamaica, formed in 1966 by brothers Jackie and Footy Bernard with Lloyd Kerr. They recorded mainly for Derrick Harriott, also working with J.J. Johnson, Leslie Kong and Rupie Edwards, and broke up in the early 1970s.

U-Roy.name: U-Roy
U-Roy.summary: Jamaican deejay Ewart Beckford (1942-2021), a pioneer of toasting over records who rose through King Tubby's sound system. His 1970 hits Wake the Town and Rule the Nation helped make deejay records commercially viable, influencing later dancehall and hip-hop artists.

studio_albums.title: Right Time Rockers - The Lost Album

Hugh Masekela.name: Hugh Masekela
Hugh Masekela.summary: South African trumpeter, flugelhornist, singer and composer (1939-2018), often called the father of South African jazz. He went into exile after the Sharpeville massacre, topped the US pop chart in 1968 with Grazing in the Grass, and wrote anti-apartheid songs such as Bring Him Back Home.

studio_albums.title: The Lasting Impression of Hugh Masekela
Hugh Masekela & The Union of South Africa
Home Is Where the Music Is
You Told Your Mama Not to Worry

Sugar Minott.name: Sugar Minott
Sugar Minott.summary: Jamaican reggae singer, producer and sound-system operator (1956-2010) who began at Studio One. He founded the Black Roots label and Youth Promotion collective and was an influential figure in the shift toward dancehall.

Wild Cherry.name: Wild Cherry
Wild Cherry.summary: Ohio funk rock band founded by Rob Parissi in 1970 and active until 1979. They are best known for Play That Funky Music, which topped the Billboard Hot 100 in 1976.

Musique.name: Musique
Musique.summary: Late-1970s New York disco studio group assembled by producer Patrick Adams, with vocalists including Jocelyn Brown and Christine Wiltshire. Their singles In the Bush and Keep On Jumpin' both reached number one on the US dance chart.

L.T.D..name: L.T.D.
L.T.D..summary: R&B and funk band from Greensboro, North Carolina, formed in 1968 and signed to A&M in 1974. With Jeffrey Osborne as lead singer they scored hits such as Love Ballad and Back in Love Again.

Delvon Lamarr Organ Trio.name: Delvon Lamarr Organ Trio
Delvon Lamarr Organ Trio.summary: Seattle soul jazz group formed in 2015 around Hammond organist Delvon Lamarr. Signed to Colemine Records, the trio mixes jazz with funk and blues influences.

Goat.name: Goat
Goat.summary: Anonymous Swedish collective that performs in masks and costumes and claims roots in the village of Korpilombolo. Recording for Rocket Recordings, they blend psychedelic and experimental rock with Afrobeat and other world music styles.

The Meters.name: The Meters
The Meters.summary: New Orleans funk band formed in 1965 that served as Allen Toussaint's house band, backing artists such as Lee Dorsey and Dr. John. Their lean, syncopated instrumentals made them a foundational funk act.

William Onyeabor.name: William Onyeabor
William Onyeabor.summary: Nigerian funk and synthesizer musician and businessman (1946-2017) from Enugu who self-released a series of albums between 1977 and 1985 before turning to Christianity and leaving music. Famously private, he found a new international audience in the 2010s through Luaka Bop reissues.

Mahalia Jackson.name: Mahalia Jackson
Mahalia Jackson.summary: Celebrated American gospel singer who recorded extensively for Columbia from the mid-1950s until her death in 1972. Her albums mixed spirituals, hymns and seasonal songs.

studio_albums.title: Great Songs of Love and Faith
Make A Joyful Noise Unto the Lord
Mahalia Jackson Sings the Best-Loved Hymns of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
Mahalia! Sings the Gospel Right out of Church

Madlib.name: Madlib
Madlib.summary: American hip hop producer, DJ and rapper Otis Jackson Jr. from Oxnard, California, known for dense sample-based beats and a long list of aliases and collaborations, including Madvillain with MF DOOM and Jaylib with J Dilla. He runs the Madlib Invazion label.

studio_albums.title: WLIB AM: King of the Wigflip

Local Natives.name: Local Natives
Local Natives.summary: American indie rock band formed in 2005 in Orange County, California, and later based in Silver Lake, Los Angeles. Built around Taylor Rice, Kelcey Ayer and Ryan Hahn, the group is known for layered vocal harmonies and percussive arrangements.

studio_albums.title: Time Will Wait for No One

Rufus Du Sol.name: Rufus Du Sol
Rufus Du Sol.summary: Australian alternative dance trio from Sydney, formed in 2010 by Tyrone Lindqvist, Jon George and James Hunt and originally known simply as Rüfüs. Their atmospheric electronic music has charted widely, and their song Alive won a Grammy for best dance/electronic recording in 2022.

World Party.name: World Party
World Party.summary: British rock act formed in London in 1986 by Karl Wallinger after he left the Waterboys, with Wallinger as essentially its only permanent member. It is best known for the international hit Ship of Fools and for She's the One, later a hit for Robbie Williams.

Sharon Van Etten.name: Sharon Van Etten
Sharon Van Etten.summary: American singer-songwriter born in 1981 in Belleville, New Jersey, whose work runs from spare indie folk to fuller, synth-driven rock. She has also acted, including a recurring part in the Netflix series The OA.

studio_albums.title: We've Been Going About This All Wrong
Sharon Van Etten & the Attachment Theory

Nick Cave & The Bad Seeds.name: Nick Cave & The Bad Seeds
Nick Cave & The Bad Seeds.summary: Rock band led by Australian singer and writer Nick Cave, formed in 1983 after the breakup of the Birthday Party. Their dark, literate songs range from post-punk noise to hushed ballads, and they have issued eighteen studio albums with a changing line-up.

studio_albums.title: Abattoir Blues / The Lyre of Orpheus

St. Paul & The Broken Bones.name: St. Paul & The Broken Bones
St. Paul & The Broken Bones.summary: A soul band formed in Birmingham, Alabama in 2012 and led by vocalist Paul Janeway. The eight-piece group plays horn-heavy Southern soul and has released six studio albums.

Charles Mingus.name: Charles Mingus
Charles Mingus.summary: American jazz double bassist, pianist, composer and bandleader (1922-1979), regarded as one of the most important jazz composers. His ambitious works, such as Mingus Ah Um and The Black Saint and the Sinner Lady, fused gospel, blues, bebop and classical ideas.

studio_albums.title: A Modern Jazz Symposium of Music and Poetry
The Black Saint and the Sinner Lady
Three or Four Shades of Blues

Abeti.name: Abeti
Abeti.summary: Congolese singer Abeti Masikini (1954-1994), born Elisabeth Finant in Stanleyville, known as the queen of soukous. She was the first Congolese woman to lead her own band, Les Redoutables, performed at the Olympia in Paris and Carnegie Hall, and appeared at the Zaire 74 festival.

studio_albums.title: Abeti & Eyenga Moseka: The Duo of the Century

Junior Vasquez.name: Junior Vasquez
Junior Vasquez.summary: American club DJ, producer and remixer born Donald Gregory Mattern in 1946 in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. He was resident DJ at New York's Sound Factory from 1989 to 1995 and remixed songs for Madonna, before a public rift with her in 1996.

Antonín Dvořák.name: Antonín Dvořák
Antonín Dvořák.summary: Czech Romantic composer (1841-1904) who drew on Bohemian and Moravian folk traditions. He wrote nine symphonies, including the New World Symphony, along with concertos, chamber works, operas and choral music, and spent several years directing a conservatory in New York.

Coolio.name: Coolio
Coolio.summary: An American rapper from Los Angeles who rose to fame in the mid-1990s. His song Gangsta's Paradise topped the Billboard Hot 100 and won a Grammy award.

Glass Animals.name: Glass Animals
Glass Animals.summary: An English indie rock band from Oxford fronted by singer and producer Dave Bayley. Their 2020 album Dreamland and its single Heat Waves brought them wide international success.

studio_albums.title: How to Be a Human Being
I Love You So F***ing Much

Nirvana.name: Nirvana
Nirvana.summary: An American rock band formed in Aberdeen, Washington in 1987 and led by Kurt Cobain. Their album Nevermind made grunge a mainstream phenomenon, and the group ended after Cobain's death in 1994.

Charles Kuralt.name: Charles Kuralt
Charles Kuralt.summary: American CBS News journalist (1934-1997) from North Carolina, known for his On the Road reports and as the first anchor of CBS News Sunday Morning. He won Peabody and Emmy awards and received Grammy awards for spoken-word recordings.

King Tubby Meets The Upsetter.name: King Tubby Meets The Upsetter
King Tubby Meets The Upsetter.summary: A billing pairing Jamaican dub engineer King Tubby with producer Lee Scratch Perry, known as the Upsetter. It is linked to the 1974 instrumental dub LP At the Grass Roots of Dub, produced by Winston Edwards, on which Tubby mixed one side and Perry the other.

Ghost Funk Orchestra.name: Ghost Funk Orchestra
Ghost Funk Orchestra.summary: A New York City band led by producer and multi-instrumentalist Seth Applebaum, which started as his solo recording project and grew into a large live ensemble. Their psychedelic funk and soul releases have come out through Colemine Records and its Karma Chief imprint.

Peter Tosh.name: Peter Tosh
Peter Tosh.summary: A Jamaican reggae singer and guitarist who was a founding member of the Wailers before launching a solo career in the 1970s. He was known for militant, outspoken songs and died in 1987.

Nick Drake.name: Nick Drake
Nick Drake.summary: An English folk singer-songwriter born in Burma in 1948 who died in 1974. He released three albums that sold poorly in his lifetime but later gained a large following and critical acclaim.

Peter Gabriel.name: Peter Gabriel
Peter Gabriel.summary: An English singer and songwriter who first came to prominence as lead vocalist of Genesis before leaving in 1975 for a solo career. His 1986 album So was his biggest commercial success.

The Grease Traps.name: The Grease Traps
The Grease Traps.summary: A deep funk and soul band from Oakland, California, whose roots go back to 2000 and which took its current form around 2005. After a run of 45 rpm singles, they released their first full-length album, Solid Ground, on Record Kicks in November 2021.

ZZ Top.name: ZZ Top
ZZ Top.summary: American rock band formed in Houston, Texas, in 1969, long made up of Billy Gibbons, Dusty Hill and Frank Beard. Known for blues-based boogie rock and their long beards, they peaked commercially in the 1980s with the synth-tinged album Eliminator.

Del Jones' Positive Vibes.name: Del Jones' Positive Vibes
Del Jones' Positive Vibes.summary: The Philadelphia group led by Del Jones, a West Philadelphia bandleader, early rapper and political activist who died in 2006. In 1973 he released two albums on his own Hikeka label, both later reissued by Now-Again Records.

Jackie Mittoo.name: Jackie Mittoo
Jackie Mittoo.summary: Jamaican keyboardist, songwriter and arranger (1948-1990) who was a founding member of the Skatalites and musical director at Studio One, where he shaped many ska, rocksteady and reggae rhythms. He later moved to Toronto and kept recording until his death in 1990.

Dirty Honey.name: Dirty Honey
Dirty Honey.summary: A hard rock band formed in Los Angeles in 2017, fronted by singer Marc LaBelle with guitarist John Notto. They put out a self-titled EP in 2019 before releasing full-length albums.

Mikey Dread.name: Mikey Dread
Mikey Dread.summary: Michael George Campbell (1954-2008) was a Jamaican broadcaster, singer and producer who hosted the JBC radio show Dread at the Controls. He later worked with the Clash, producing their single Bankrobber and appearing on Sandinista!

studio_albums.title: Come to Mikey Dread's Dub Party

Björk.name: Björk
Björk.summary: Icelandic singer, songwriter and producer who first gained international attention with the Sugarcubes before launching a solo career in 1993. Her work mixes electronic, orchestral and avant-garde elements and is known for ambitious visual and multimedia projects.

Warpaint.name: Warpaint
Warpaint.summary: An indie rock band formed in Los Angeles in 2004, featuring Emily Kokal, Theresa Wayman, Jenny Lee Lindberg and drummer Stella Mozgawa, who joined in 2009. They have released four studio albums.

Slade.name: Slade
Slade.summary: A British rock band that started out as Ambrose Slade and issued fifteen studio albums between 1969 and 1994, the final one under the name Slade II. Their 1972 concert album Slade Alive! was a major chart success.

Barry White.name: Barry White
Barry White.summary: American singer, songwriter and producer (1944-2003) famed for his deep bass voice and lush orchestrated soul and disco. He led the Love Unlimited Orchestra and scored hits such as Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe and You're the First, the Last, My Everything.

studio_albums.title: I've Got So Much to Give
Just Another Way to Say I Love You
Barry White Sings for Someone You Love
I Love to Sing the Songs I Sing

His Eyes Have Fangs.name: His Eyes Have Fangs
His Eyes Have Fangs.summary: A Los Angeles music project credited to skateboarding pioneer Tony Alva together with Matthew and Rachel Anne Rainwater. Its self-described neo-noir dream rock draws on surf, psychedelic and ambient styles, with releases appearing on Bandcamp from 2013 onward.

Waylon Jennings & Willie Nelson.name: Waylon Jennings & Willie Nelson
Waylon Jennings & Willie Nelson.summary: A joint billing of country singers Waylon Jennings and Willie Nelson, central figures of the 1970s outlaw country movement. Besides solo careers, they recorded several duet albums, starting with Waylon & Willie in 1978, and later joined Johnny Cash and Kris Kristofferson in the Highwaymen.

studio_albums.title: Are You Ready for the Country
Too Dumb for New York City, Too Ugly for L.A.
Goin' Down Rockin': The Last Recordings

Derek And The Dominos.name: Derek And The Dominos
Derek And The Dominos.summary: A short-lived rock group led by Eric Clapton with Bobby Whitlock, Carl Radle and Jim Gordon, first performing under that name in August 1970. Their only studio record, featuring Duane Allman as guest guitarist, was followed by a US tour later that year.

studio_albums.title: Layla and Other Assorted Love Songs

The Roots.name: The Roots
The Roots.summary: A Philadelphia hip-hop band formed in 1987 by Black Thought and Questlove, notable for using live instruments and a jazz-influenced style. They have served as the house band for Jimmy Fallon's NBC late-night shows since 2009 and won a Grammy in 2000.

Roosevelt.name: Roosevelt
Roosevelt.summary: Roosevelt is the performing name of Marius Lauber, a German singer, songwriter, DJ and producer born in 1990 in Viersen. He makes synth-pop and indie electronic music and has released records through labels including Greco-Roman and City Slang.

Aaron Dessner & Bryce Dessner.name: Aaron Dessner & Bryce Dessner
Aaron Dessner & Bryce Dessner.summary: Twin brothers from Cincinnati who play guitar and keyboards in the rock band the National. Working as a pair, they have composed and produced together on film scores such as Cyrano and on projects like the Day of the Dead tribute; Aaron is also known as a producer for Taylor Swift.

Sparks.name: Sparks
Sparks.summary: An American duo of brothers Ron and Russell Mael, formed in Los Angeles in 1970 under the name Halfnelson. Known for witty, offbeat songwriting, they broke through in the UK with Kimono My House in 1974 and have released more than two dozen studio albums.

studio_albums.title: Pulling Rabbits Out of a Hat
Music That You Can Dance To
The Girl Is Crying in Her Latte

Foals.name: Foals
Foals.summary: English rock band formed in Oxford in 2005, fronted by singer and guitarist Yannis Philippakis. Starting out with angular math rock, they moved toward broader, more anthemic indie rock and have received several Mercury Prize nominations.

studio_albums.title: Everything Not Saved Will Be Lost – Part 1
Everything Not Saved Will Be Lost – Part 2

Taylor Swift.name: Taylor Swift
Taylor Swift.summary: American singer-songwriter who began in country music in Nashville before moving into pop, folk-influenced and synth-pop styles. She is one of the best-selling musicians in history, has won numerous Grammys, and re-recorded her early albums after a dispute over her master recordings.

Wire.name: Wire
Wire.summary: An English band formed in London in 1976, associated with punk, post-punk and art punk. Their debut Pink Flag and the more experimental follow-ups Chairs Missing and 154 made them highly influential, and the group has continued recording into the 21st century.

studio_albums.title: A Bell Is a Cup... Until It Is Struck
It's Beginning to and Back Again

Neil Young.name: Neil Young
Neil Young.summary: Canadian-American singer-songwriter and guitarist whose career began with Buffalo Springfield and Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young. Alternating between gentle folk-country and loud, distorted rock, often with Crazy Horse, he is among the most prolific and influential rock musicians.

Elvis Presley.name: Elvis Presley
Elvis Presley.summary: American singer and actor (1935-1977) widely called the King of Rock and Roll. Emerging from Memphis in the mid-1950s, he blended country, blues and gospel into a hugely popular style, starred in many films and became one of the best-selling solo artists ever.

studio_albums.title: Elvis Sings The Wonderful World of Christmas
Raised on Rock / For Ol' Times Sake
From Elvis Presley Boulevard, Memphis, Tennessee

Neil Young & Crazy Horse.name: Neil Young & Crazy Horse
Neil Young & Crazy Horse.summary: The long-running partnership between Neil Young and his backing band Crazy Horse, whose loose, loud garage-rock sound first appeared on Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere in 1969. Their joint records include Zuma, Rust Never Sleeps, Ragged Glory and later albums such as Barn.

The Cult.name: The Cult
The Cult.summary: An obscure American funk group of the 1970s whose only known album, The Mail Must Go Through, came out in 1976 on Starburst Records, a label apparently based in Las Vegas. The record became a sought-after collectible and was reissued in 2021.

Coldplay.name: Coldplay
Coldplay.summary: British rock band formed in London in 1997, led by singer Chris Martin with Jonny Buckland, Guy Berryman and Will Champion. Known for anthemic pop-rock and large stadium tours, they are among the best-selling groups of the 21st century.

studio_albums.title: A Rush of Blood to the Head
Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends

Lou Reed.name: Lou Reed
Lou Reed.summary: American singer and songwriter who first came to attention with the Velvet Underground before a long solo career beginning in 1972. His late-1980s album New York revived his critical standing.

Art Blakey & The Jazz Messengers.name: Art Blakey & The Jazz Messengers
Art Blakey & The Jazz Messengers.summary: The hard bop ensemble led by drummer Art Blakey from the mid-1950s until his death in 1990. It served as a training ground for young players, with alumni including Lee Morgan, Wayne Shorter, Freddie Hubbard and Wynton Marsalis.

studio_albums.title: I Get a Kick Out of Bu

Alicia Keys.name: Alicia Keys
Alicia Keys.summary: American singer, songwriter and classically trained pianist from New York who debuted in 2001 with Songs in A Minor. Combining R&B, soul and piano-based pop, she has won many Grammy awards and also co-created the Broadway musical Hell's Kitchen.

Metallica.name: Metallica
Metallica.summary: American heavy metal band formed in Los Angeles in 1981 by James Hetfield and Lars Ulrich. Pioneers of thrash metal, they reached a mass audience with their 1991 self-titled record and rank among the best-selling bands in history.

The Cranberries.name: The Cranberries
The Cranberries.summary: Irish rock band formed in Limerick in 1989, with Dolores O'Riordan joining as singer in 1990. One of the most commercially successful alternative acts of the 1990s, they split after O'Riordan's death in 2018 and a final album in 2019.

studio_albums.title: Everybody Else Is Doing It, So Why Can't We?
Wake Up and Smell the Coffee

Sinéad O'Connor.name: Sinéad O'Connor
Sinéad O'Connor.summary: Irish singer-songwriter who released ten studio albums from 1987 onward. Her 1997 hits collection drew on her early records and was her final release for Chrysalis.

studio_albums.title: I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got
How About I Be Me (and You Be You)?
I'm Not Bossy, I'm the Boss

Alabama Shakes.name: Alabama Shakes
Alabama Shakes.summary: American rock quartet fronted by singer and guitarist Brittany Howard, blending soul, blues and Southern rock. Their second album Sound & Color reached number one in the US and won multiple Grammys.

Pixies.name: Pixies
Pixies.summary: Alternative rock band formed in Boston in 1986 by Black Francis, Joey Santiago, Kim Deal and David Lovering, known for abrupt quiet-loud dynamics. They split in 1993, reunited in 2004, and have continued recording with later bassists.

Reverb Motherfuckers.name: Reverb Motherfuckers
Reverb Motherfuckers.summary: A New York noise-punk group of the late 1980s that styled its music as scum rock. Critics likened their chaotic, jokey guitar noise to Shockabilly and Adrenalin O.D.

studio_albums.title: Twelve Swinging Signs of the Zodiac

Morrissey.name: Morrissey
Morrissey.summary: English singer and lyricist who fronted the Smiths in the 1980s before launching a solo career in 1988. His work is known for its witty, melancholic lyrics and distinctive croon, while his public statements have often drawn controversy.

studio_albums.title: World Peace Is None of Your Business
I Am Not a Dog on a Chain

Ramones.name: Ramones
Ramones.summary: American punk rock band from Queens, New York, formed in 1974, whose short, fast, stripped-down songs helped launch the punk movement. Members adopted the Ramone surname, and the group toured relentlessly until disbanding in 1996.

Skin Alley.name: Skin Alley
Skin Alley.summary: A London progressive rock band active from 1968 to 1974 that mixed prog with jazz-rock and folk elements. They released four albums on CBS and then Transatlantic.

Smegma.name: Smegma
Smegma.summary: American experimental noise and free improvisation collective formed in Pasadena, California, in 1973, later based in Portland, Oregon. With a rotating membership that came to include writer Richard Meltzer, the group has released records for decades and appeared on the Nurse with Wound list.

Fun..name: Fun.
Fun..summary: American pop rock band formed in New York in 2008 by Nate Ruess, Andrew Dost and Jack Antonoff. Their second album Some Nights brought the number-one hit We Are Young, and the group went on hiatus in 2015.

The Slickee Boys.name: The Slickee Boys
The Slickee Boys.summary: Garage, punk and psychedelic rock band from the Washington, D.C. area, active from 1976 to 1991. They were a fixture of the local punk scene, known for energetic shows and for mixing originals with covers of obscure 1960s songs.

Romeo Void.name: Romeo Void
Romeo Void.summary: San Francisco new wave and post-punk band fronted by singer Debora Iyall, active mainly from 1979 to 1985. They are best remembered for Never Say Never and for A Girl in Trouble (Is a Temporary Thing), which became a top 40 pop hit.

Chvrches.name: Chvrches
Chvrches.summary: Scottish synth-pop trio formed in Glasgow in 2011, consisting of singer Lauren Mayberry with Iain Cook and Martin Doherty. Their bright, electronic pop first gained attention online with The Mother We Share.

studio_albums.title: The Bones of What You Believe

Muse.name: Muse
Muse.summary: English rock band from Teignmouth, Devon, formed in 1994 by Matt Bellamy, Chris Wolstenholme and Dominic Howard. They blend alternative rock with electronic, classical and progressive elements and are noted for elaborate, theatrical live shows.

Charli XCX.name: Charli XCX
Charli XCX.summary: English singer and songwriter who broke through with Boom Clap and guest spots on hits by Icona Pop and Iggy Azalea. From the mid-2010s she moved toward experimental electronic pop, alongside several mixtapes.

Charlotte Adigéry & Bolis Pupul.name: Charlotte Adigéry & Bolis Pupul
Charlotte Adigéry & Bolis Pupul.summary: A Belgian duo pairing singer Charlotte Adigéry with producer Bolis Pupul, both of Martinican heritage, who met while working on a Soulwax film soundtrack. After Pupul produced her EPs on Deewee, the pair released their joint album Topical Dancer in 2022.

Television.name: Television
Television.summary: New York band formed in 1973 around Tom Verlaine and Richard Lloyd that became a fixture at CBGB. Their intricate, improvisational guitar rock influenced punk and alternative music; they split in 1978, reunited in 1992 and played occasionally afterwards.

Joy Division.name: Joy Division
Joy Division.summary: Post-punk band formed in Salford in 1976 by Bernard Sumner, Peter Hook, Ian Curtis and Stephen Morris, first known as Warsaw. After Curtis died in May 1980 the remaining members continued as New Order.

Fugazi.name: Fugazi
Fugazi.summary: Washington, D.C. post-hardcore band featuring Ian MacKaye, Guy Picciotto, Joe Lally and Brendan Canty, who released their records on the independent Dischord label. They issued six studio albums between 1990 and 2001.

Patti Smith.name: Patti Smith
Patti Smith.summary: American singer, songwriter, poet and author whose 1975 debut Horses fused rock with poetry and influenced the New York punk scene. She is also known for her memoir Just Kids and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2007.

The Slits.name: The Slits
The Slits.summary: London punk band founded in 1976 by Ari Up and Palmolive, later including Viv Albertine and Tessa Pollitt. Their sound shifted from raw punk toward reggae and dub influences; active until 1982, they regrouped from 2005 to 2010.

PJ Harvey.name: PJ Harvey
PJ Harvey.summary: English singer-songwriter Polly Jean Harvey, who debuted in 1992 with Dry on Too Pure. She has released ten solo studio albums and two collaborative records with John Parish.

studio_albums.title: Stories from the City, Stories from the Sea
I Inside the Old Year Dying

Panic! At The Disco.name: Panic! At The Disco
Panic! At The Disco.summary: Las Vegas pop rock act started in 2004 by school friends including Ryan Ross, Spencer Smith and Brendon Urie. After many lineup changes it became Urie's solo vehicle from 2015, and he ended the project in 2023.

studio_albums.title: A Fever You Can't Sweat Out
Too Weird to Live, Too Rare to Die!

Toots And The Maytals.name: Toots And The Maytals
Toots And The Maytals.summary: Jamaican vocal group led by Frederick Toots Hibbert, formed in the early 1960s and central to the development of ska, rocksteady and reggae. Their 1968 song Do the Reggay is credited with naming the genre, and hits include Pressure Drop and 54-46 That's My Number.

Gang Of Four.name: Gang Of Four
Gang Of Four.summary: English post-punk band formed in Leeds in 1976 by Jon King, Andy Gill, Hugo Burnham and Dave Allen. They combined punk with funk and dub and wrote pointedly political lyrics, influencing later dance-punk acts.

The Mono Men.name: The Mono Men
The Mono Men.summary: Garage punk band from Bellingham, Washington, active from 1987 to 1998 with later reunions, led by Dave Crider. Mostly recording for Estrus, they paired fuzzed-out guitars with the 1960s Northwest garage sound of acts like the Sonics.

Germs.name: Germs
Germs.summary: Los Angeles punk band formed in 1976, best known for singer Darby Crash, guitarist Pat Smear, bassist Lorna Doom and drummer Don Bolles. They released one studio album before Crash's death in 1980 ended the group, later reuniting briefly in the 2000s.

Wet Leg.name: Wet Leg
Wet Leg.summary: Indie rock band from the Isle of Wight, formed in 2019 around Rhian Teasdale and Hester Chambers. Their debut album topped the UK chart and won two Grammys, and they also took Brit Awards for Best New Artist and Best British Group.

Devo.name: Devo
Devo.summary: New wave band formed in Akron, Ohio, in 1973, built around the Mothersbaugh and Casale brothers. Their name and outlook come from the satirical idea of de-evolution, and their best-known song, Whip It, was their only US Top 40 hit.

studio_albums.title: Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!

Joan Jett And The Blackhearts.name: Joan Jett And The Blackhearts
Joan Jett And The Blackhearts.summary: American rock band led by former Runaways guitarist and singer Joan Jett, formed at the end of the 1970s with producer Kenny Laguna as her longtime partner. Their cover of I Love Rock 'n' Roll became a major US number one in 1982.

studio_albums.title: Glorious Results of a Misspent Youth

The Replacements.name: The Replacements
The Replacements.summary: Minneapolis rock band led by Paul Westerberg with Tommy and Bob Stinson and Chris Mars, active from around 1979 to 1991. Influential in alternative rock, they moved from raw punk to more melodic records and later reunited between 2012 and 2015.

studio_albums.title: Sorry Ma, Forgot to Take Out the Trash

Norah Jones.name: Norah Jones
Norah Jones.summary: American singer, songwriter and pianist whose jazz-tinged debut Come Away with Me became one of the best-selling albums of the 2000s and won multiple Grammys. She has since explored country, pop and rock styles, both solo and in collaborative projects.

studio_albums.title: Pick Me Up Off the Floor

Toots & The Maytals.name: Toots & The Maytals
Toots & The Maytals.summary: Jamaican vocal group fronted by Toots Hibbert, active from the early 1960s through ska, rocksteady and reggae. Their 1968 song Do the Reggay helped give the genre its name, and the group remained active until Hibbert's death in 2020.

Lee Perry And His Upsetters.name: Lee Perry And His Upsetters
Lee Perry And His Upsetters.summary: Billing for Jamaican producer Lee Scratch Perry together with the Upsetters, the studio band he assembled after founding Upsetter Records in 1968. Perry, who died in 2021, built the Black Ark studio in 1973 and is credited as a key pioneer of dub.
