Desmond Dekker.name: Desmond Dekker
Desmond Dekker.summary: Jamaican ska, rocksteady and reggae singer born Desmond Dacres in 1941, who recorded with his group the Aces. His 1968 song Israelites topped the UK chart and reached the US top ten; he settled in England and died in London in 2006.

studio_albums.title: You Can Get It If You Really Want

Toro Y Moi.name: Toro Y Moi
Toro Y Moi.summary: Recording name of American musician Chaz Bear, born Chazwick Bundick in South Carolina and now based in the San Francisco Bay Area. He is regarded as an early figure of the chillwave scene and has since moved through funk, house and psychedelic styles.

Nas.name: Nas
Nas.summary: American rapper from Queens, New York, whose 1994 debut Illmatic is regarded as one of the defining hip-hop albums. He has released many solo albums since, including a late-career run of records produced by Hit-Boy, and collaborations with Damian Marley and DJ Premier.

UB40.name: UB40
UB40.summary: Reggae and dub band formed in Birmingham in 1978, named after a British unemployment benefit form. They have had more than 50 UK hit singles, including Red Red Wine, which also topped the US chart, and have sold over 100 million records.

Buzzcocks.name: Buzzcocks
Buzzcocks.summary: English punk band formed in the Manchester area in 1976 by Pete Shelley and Howard Devoto. Known for sharp, melodic pop-punk singles such as Ever Fallen in Love, they split in 1981, re-formed in 1989 and continued recording in later decades.

studio_albums.title: Another Music in a Different Kitchen

Muddy Waters.name: Muddy Waters
Muddy Waters.summary: Mississippi-born blues singer and guitarist, born McKinley Morganfield, who became a central figure of Chicago electric blues through his recordings for Chess Records. His amplified band sound strongly shaped later rock musicians, and he died in 1983.

Ngozi Family.name: Ngozi Family
Ngozi Family.summary: Zambian rock group of the 1970s led by singer and guitarist Paul Ngozi, one of the first acts labelled Zamrock. Their fuzz-heavy records addressed everyday social issues and have been reissued internationally in recent years.

Witch.name: Witch
Witch.summary: Witch is a Zambian rock band fronted by singer Emanuel Jagari Chanda, active from the early 1970s into the mid-1980s and revived in 2012. They were central to Zamrock, mixing psychedelic and garage rock with funk and later disco and kalindula.

Childish Gambino.name: Childish Gambino
Childish Gambino.summary: Childish Gambino is the music project of American actor, writer and comedian Donald Glover. Starting in hip-hop, he later moved toward funk, soul and R&B, and his 2018 single This Is America won several Grammy Awards.

John Cougar.name: John Cougar
John Cougar.summary: John Cougar was the stage name used early in his career by John Mellencamp, a heartland rock singer-songwriter born in 1951 in Seymour, Indiana. He later billed himself as John Cougar Mellencamp and then by his real name, and joined the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2008.

studio_albums.title: Nothin' Matters and What If It Did

Steve Martin.name: Steve Martin
Steve Martin.summary: Steve Martin, born in 1945 in Waco, Texas, is an American comedian, actor, writer and banjo player. He was a leading stand-up act of the 1970s with hit comedy records, then moved into films and later released bluegrass albums, winning Grammys for both comedy and music.

studio_albums.title: The Crow: New Songs for the 5-String Banjo

Steve Winwood.name: Steve Winwood
Steve Winwood.summary: Steve Winwood is an English singer and multi-instrumentalist who first found fame as a teenager in the Spencer Davis Group, then co-founded Traffic and Blind Faith. His solo career peaked in the 1980s with records such as Back in the High Life.

The Smithereens.name: The Smithereens
The Smithereens.summary: The Smithereens are an American rock band formed in 1980 in Carteret, New Jersey. Known for power pop shaped by 1960s influences, they had late-1980s hits with Pat DiNizio as frontman, and continued after his death in 2017.

Dusty Springfield.name: Dusty Springfield
Dusty Springfield.summary: Dusty Springfield was an English pop and soul singer who rose to fame in the 1960s with hits such as I Only Want to Be with You and Son of a Preacher Man. Her 1969 album Dusty in Memphis is regarded as a classic, and she later revived her career alongside the Pet Shop Boys.

studio_albums.title: Stay Awhile/I Only Want to Be with You
You Don't Have to Say You Love Me

Ferry Djimmy and his Dji-Kins.name: Ferry Djimmy and his Dji-Kins
Ferry Djimmy and his Dji-Kins.summary: Ferry Djimmy, born Jean Maurille Ogoudjobi in 1939, was a Beninese bandleader who recorded Afrobeat and funk with his backing group the Dji-Kins in the 1970s. He later settled in Lagos, Nigeria, where he died in 1996.

Al Di Meola, John McLaughlin & Paco De L.name: Al Di Meola, John McLaughlin & Paco De Lucía
Al Di Meola, John McLaughlin & Paco De L.summary: This billing names a guitar trio formed by American jazz fusion player Al Di Meola, English guitarist John McLaughlin and Spanish flamenco guitarist Paco de Lucia. They toured together in the early 1980s, and their San Francisco concerts produced the celebrated Friday Night in San Francisco recording.

studio_albums.title: World Sinfonia II – Heart of the Immigrants
World Sinfonía III - The Grande Passion
Diabolic Inventions and Seduction For Solo Guitar
All Your Life (A Tribute to the Beatles)

The Notorious B.I.G..name: The Notorious B.I.G.
The Notorious B.I.G..summary: Brooklyn rapper Christopher Wallace, known as Biggie Smalls, was a leading figure of 1990s East Coast hip-hop on Bad Boy Records. He was shot dead in Los Angeles in 1997, shortly before his second album came out.

Moby.name: Moby
Moby.summary: Moby, born Richard Melville Hall, is a New York electronic musician, producer and DJ who emerged from the early 1990s rave scene. His 1999 album Play became a global commercial success, and he has released a long run of dance, rock and ambient records since.

studio_albums.title: More Fast Songs About the Apocalypse
Everything Was Beautiful, and Nothing Hurt

Muddy Waters & The Rolling Stones.name: Muddy Waters & The Rolling Stones
Muddy Waters & The Rolling Stones.summary: A one-off joint billing for a November 1981 performance at Chicago's Checkerboard Lounge, where Rolling Stones members Mick Jagger, Keith Richards and Ronnie Wood sat in with blues pioneer Muddy Waters and his band. The Stones had taken their name from a Waters song.

Elvis Costello.name: Elvis Costello
Elvis Costello.summary: Elvis Costello, born Declan MacManus, is an English singer-songwriter who came to prominence in the late 1970s new wave scene, often backed by the Attractions. Across a long career he has worked in many styles, including country, classical and soul, and collaborated with artists such as Burt Bacharach.

Dead Kennedys.name: Dead Kennedys
Dead Kennedys.summary: Dead Kennedys were a San Francisco punk band formed in 1978, fronted by Jello Biafra, and known for sharp political satire. They released four studio albums before splitting in 1986, and later re-formed without Biafra after a legal dispute with him.

Wilco.name: Wilco
Wilco.summary: Wilco is a Chicago rock band formed in 1994 by Jeff Tweedy after the breakup of Uncle Tupelo. Starting from alternative country, the group moved toward more experimental rock, with Yankee Hotel Foxtrot becoming its best-known record.

Chris Isaak.name: Chris Isaak
Chris Isaak.summary: American singer, songwriter and actor from Stockton, California, known for a reverb-drenched style rooted in rockabilly and 1950s pop. His 1989 song Wicked Game became his signature hit, and he has acted in films such as Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me and hosted his own TV shows.

Willie Nelson & Family.name: Willie Nelson & Family
Willie Nelson & Family.summary: Billing for country star Willie Nelson together with the Family, his long-running backing band formed in the 1970s after he signed with Atlantic. Nelson, a Texas-born singer-songwriter and outlaw country figure, has recorded prolifically for over six decades and starred in the film Honeysuckle Rose.

The IRS Tapes: Who'll Buy My Memories?
Run That by Me One More Time
You Don't Know Me: The Songs of Cindy Walker
Let's Face the Music and Dance
For the Good Times: A Tribute to Ray Price
Willie and the Boys: Willie's Stash, Vol. 2
I Don't Know a Thing About Love

Florence and The Machine.name: Florence and The Machine
Florence and The Machine.summary: English band formed in London in 2007, fronted by singer Florence Welch, blending indie rock, baroque pop and soul. Their debut Lungs topped the UK chart and won a Brit Award, and later albums such as How Big, How Blue, How Beautiful reached number one in the US.

studio_albums.title: How Big, How Blue, How Beautiful

Larry Raspberry And The Highsteppers.name: Larry Raspberry And The Highsteppers
Larry Raspberry And The Highsteppers.summary: Memphis rock and soul band started in 1969 by Larry Raspberry, formerly of the 1960s group the Gentrys. The group toured widely, released LPs in the 1970s including one on the Stax-affiliated Enterprise label, and was later honored with a Beale Street Walk of Fame note.

San Francisco 49ers.name: San Francisco 49ers
San Francisco 49ers.summary: Professional American football franchise in the NFL, based in the San Francisco Bay Area and playing in Santa Clara. The team won its first Super Bowl, Super Bowl XVI, after the 1981 season and has won five Super Bowls in total.

Karyn White.name: Karyn White
Karyn White.summary: American R&B singer and songwriter born in Los Angeles in 1965, popular in the late 1980s and early 1990s on Warner Bros. Her hits include Superwoman, The Way You Love Me and the US number one Romantic, and she returned in 2012 after a long hiatus.

Chet Baker, Art Pepper & Phil Urso.name: Chet Baker, Art Pepper & Phil Urso
Chet Baker, Art Pepper & Phil Urso.summary: Joint billing for a 1956 West Coast jazz session led by trumpeter Chet Baker and alto saxophonist Art Pepper, with Phil Urso on tenor saxophone. Released by Pacific Jazz as Playboys and later reissued as Picture of Heath, it was one of several Baker and Pepper collaborations that year.

Kate Bush.name: Kate Bush
Kate Bush.summary: English singer, songwriter and producer born in 1958 who broke through as a teenager with Wuthering Heights in 1978. Known for theatrical, inventive art pop, she achieved her greatest success with Hounds of Love and its single Running Up That Hill.

Tom Petty And The Heartbreakers.name: Tom Petty And The Heartbreakers
Tom Petty And The Heartbreakers.summary: American rock band led by singer-songwriter Tom Petty, formed in 1976 with guitarist Mike Campbell and keyboardist Benmont Tench among its core members. Known for heartland rock hits such as Refugee and The Waiting, the group entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2002 and stopped after Petty died in 2017.

studio_albums.title: Songs and Music from "She's the One"

Yaz.name: Yaz
Yaz.summary: English synth-pop duo of singer Alison Moyet and keyboardist Vince Clarke, formed in Basildon in 1981 and billed as Yaz in North America because another act already used the name Yazoo. Active until 1983, with later reunions, they scored UK hits including Only You, Don't Go and Nobody's Diary.

Neil Young With Crazy Horse.name: Neil Young With Crazy Horse
Neil Young With Crazy Horse.summary: Joint billing of Canadian-American singer-songwriter Neil Young and Crazy Horse, the Los Angeles band that has backed him since 1969 with Billy Talbot and Ralph Molina at its core. Their partnership is known for loud, extended guitar rock on records such as Zuma, Rust Never Sleeps and Ragged Glory.

The Linda Lindas.name: The Linda Lindas
The Linda Lindas.summary: Punk rock band from Los Angeles formed in 2018 by sisters Lucia and Mila de la Garza, their cousin Eloise Wong and friend Bela Salazar. A 2021 library performance of Racist, Sexist Boy went viral, leading to a deal with Epitaph Records.

Freddie Gibbs & Madlib.name: Freddie Gibbs & Madlib
Freddie Gibbs & Madlib.summary: Hip-hop partnership between Indiana rapper Freddie Gibbs and California producer Madlib, sometimes called MadGibbs. Pairing Gibbs's street-focused rhymes with Madlib's sample-based beats, the duo released the albums Piñata in 2014 and Bandana in 2019.

Green Day.name: Green Day
Green Day.summary: American rock band formed in the East Bay area of California in 1987, led by Billie Joe Armstrong with Mike Dirnt and Tré Cool. They helped popularize pop punk with Dookie, reinvented themselves with the rock opera American Idiot, and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2015.

The Postal Service.name: The Postal Service
The Postal Service.summary: American indie electronic duo of singer Ben Gibbard and producer Jimmy Tamborello, with Jenny Lewis contributing vocals. Its name comes from the pair swapping recordings by mail while making their sole album, Give Up, released by Sub Pop in 2003.
